work: Pausanias' description of Greece, Volume I. + II.

Hercules.what: Hercules' lion skin fails to frighten young Theseus at Troezen.
Hercules feuds with Hippocoon and his sons, takes vengeance, and builds a temple to Athene.
Hercules clears Augeas' dung with a river but is cheated of his reward.
Hercules ambushes and kills the sons of Actor at Cleonæ.
Hercules sacks Elis, spares Pisa by oracle, and gives Elis to Phyleus.
Hercules rescues Phialo and her baby after the jay's cry.

Apollo.what: Apollo lays his harp on a stone while helping Alcathous build the wall.
Apollo fathers Æsculapius, who is exposed on the mountain.
Apollo, jealous, causes Leucippus to be exposed and killed.
Apollo and Artemis visit Tegea, where Limon kills Scephrus.
Apollo kills Caanthus, who burned his grove seeking Melia.
Apollo kills the dragon at Pytho and fathers Lycorus and Delphus.

Zeus.what: Zeus' statue by Phidias is seated on its richly adorned throne at Olympia.
Lycaon sacrifices a baby to Lycæan Zeus and is turned into a wolf.
Zeus loves Callisto, who is turned into a bear by Hera.
Zeus follows Cithæron's advice and parades a wooden statue as bride to Hera.
Zeus is saved as an infant when Cronos swallows a stone.

Athene.what: Athene's gold and ivory statue stands in the Parthenon.
Athene contests Attica with Poseidon; her ancient statue and golden lamp are honoured.
Athene receives a temple built by Hercules after his vengeance.
Athene is wounded in the thigh by Teuthis at Aulis.

Artemis.what: Artemis misleads Mardonius' men, who are slain by Megarians.
Artemis, angered by profanation, sends famine and plague on Patræ.
Artemis shoots Callisto, who has been turned into a bear.
Artemis sends Chronius a dream to avenge a maiden.
Artemis shoots Limon after he kills Scephrus.

Poseidon.what: Poseidon contests Attica with Athene and marks the rock with his trident.
Poseidon loses the land dispute and dries up the rivers.
Poseidon lies with Æthra and exchanges Calaurea for Delphi.
Poseidon destroys Helice after the Achæans kill suppliants.
Poseidon pursues Demeter in horse form and fathers Arion.

Dionysus.what: Semele and infant Dionysus wash ashore at Brasiae and are nursed.
Dionysus sends madness on Calydon after Coresus' prayer.

Demeter.what: Demeter gives Phytalus the fig tree.
Demeter sits at the well as an old woman.
Demeter's temple at Hermione is founded by Chthonia after Colontas refuses her hospitality.
Demeter, assaulted by Poseidon, is worshipped as Erinys and Lusia.
Demeter hides in the cave in mourning until Pan reveals her.

Aphrodite.what: Aphrodite turns Selemnus into a river and gives him forgetfulness.
Aphrodite is named mother of Eros by most.

Hermes.what: Hermes plucks the child Æsculapius from the pyre.
Hermes saves Callisto's child at Zeus' bidding.
Nymphs wash infant Hermes at the Tricrena wells.
Hermes makes a lyre from a tortoise on Chelydorea.

Æsculapius.what: Æsculapius comes to Sicyon from Epidaurus as a dragon.
Æsculapius is born, exposed, and protected by a goat and dog.
Epidaurians settle Epidaurus Limera after Æsculapius' dragon escapes.
Æsculapius cures Phalysius of blindness by a sealed letter.

Philip.what: Philip poisons Aratus and two Athenian orators.
Philip helps the Messenians and corrupts Elis with bribes.
Philip uses bribery and poison and garrisons the keys of Greece.
Philip is beaten by the Romans at Cynoscephalae.
Philip breaks his oaths and his family's early deaths follow.
Philip ends the Sacred War and razes Phocian towns.

Hera.what: Hera wins the land of Argolis.
Hera turns Callisto into a bear.
Hera is raised at Stymphelus and given three temples.
Hera, angry with Zeus, is tricked into a sham wedding and reconciled.

Theseus.what: Theseus retrieves Minos' ring from the sea and is later killed on Scyrus.
Theseus, mocked by roof builders, throws their waggon over the roof.
Theseus lifts the stone at eighteen and sacrifices the Marathonian bull.
Theseus defeats Cercyon by skill and aids Adrastus.
Theseus throws Sciron into the sea.
Theseus clears the Isthmus road of robbers.

Alexander.what: Alexander's body is taken by Ptolemy and buried.
Younger Alexander is made king by Cleopatra and kills her.
Alexander conquers Porus and first brings elephants to Europeans.
Alexander is tricked by Anaximenes into sparing Lampsacus.
Alexander destroys Thebes after its revolt.

Homer.what: Homer is noted for never mentioning elephants.
Homer is said to describe Thamyris' blinding.
Callinus attributes the Thebais to Homer; Pausanias disagrees.
Oracles dispute Homer's birthplace at Delphi.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon swears an oath over a boar.
Agamemnon gathers Greek chiefs at Ægium.
Agamemnon's sceptre is worshipped at Chaeronea.

Pyrrhus.what: Pyrrhus allies with then is driven from Macedonia by Lysimachus.
Pyrrhus regains Epirus and is first Greek to fight Rome.
Pyrrhus crosses to Italy, routs the Romans with elephants, then goes to Sicily.
Pyrrhus escapes Italy, beats Antigonus, attacks Sparta and dies at Argos.
Pyrrhus of Pisa rebels against Elis.

Proserpine.what: Proserpine's abduction frames the Triptolemus stories.
Pluto carries off Proserpine at Lerna.
Proserpine appears to Pindar in a dream.

Achilles.what: Achilles lives on Leuce as Helen's husband.
Locals claim Achilles killed Las when wooing Helen.
Achilles is the model of speed for Theagenes.

Antigonus.what: Antigonus fights Ptolemy and is finally defeated and killed.
Antigonus is beaten by Pyrrhus in Macedonia.
Antigonus besieges Athens and imposes a garrison.
Antigonus admires the wounded Philopoemen at Sellasia.

Pollux.what: Pollux and Castor visit Phormio and vanish, leaving statues.
Messenians pose as the twins, earning their hatred.

Odysseus.what: Odysseus wins a race and dedicates Athene Celeuthea.
Odysseus' marriage to Penelope is recalled when Icarius pleads.

Orestes.what: Orestes is tried at the Areopagus for killing his mother.
Orestes' bones are found at Tegea by Lichas.
Orestes is said to have brought the Tauric statue to Sparta.
Orestes goes mad near Maniæ and is healed.

Ares.what: Ares is the first tried at the Areopagus.
Tegean women sacrifice to Ares after defeating Charillus.

Castor.what: Castor and Pollux visit Phormio and vanish, leaving statues.
Messenians pose as the twins, earning their hatred.

Xerxes.what: Xerxes carries off the bronze Apollo of Branchidæ.
Xerxes invades Greece and faces Leonidas at Thermopylæ.
Xerxes' fleet is wrecked, its cables cut by Scyllis.

Aristodemus.what: Aristodemus kills his own daughter to fulfil the oracle.
Aristodemus is elected king despite the seers' objection.
Aristodemus' tactics rout the Spartans near Ithome.
Aristodemus rejects the deserters and sets up wooden tripods.
Aristodemus kills himself at his daughter's grave.

Perseus.what: Perseus accidentally kills Acrisius and founds Mycenae.
Perseus is honoured with a chapel near Mycenae.
Perseus slays Medusa, whose grave is shown.

Aristomenes.what: Aristomenes is made king and hangs a shield in Sparta.
Aristomenes routs the Spartans, loses and recovers his shield, and seizes Caryae maidens.
Aristomenes is captured at Ægila, escapes, and holds Eira.
Aristomenes is thrown in the Ceadas and escapes following a fox.
Aristomenes destroys the Corinthians and is freed by a girl.
Aristomenes leads the survivors out of fallen Eira.

Ptolemy.what: Ptolemy takes Alexander's body, fends off Perdiccas, and fights Antigonus.
Ptolemy marries Arsinoe, kills his brothers, and strands the Galati mercenaries.

Pelops.what: Pelops deposes Oenomaus and takes Pisaea and Olympia.
Pelops is honoured at Olympia, his shoulder-blade a relic needed for Troy.
Pelops defeats Oenomaus and buries the slain suitors.
Pelops wins Hippodamia and drowns Myrtilus.

Demetrius.what: Demetrius and Antigonus defeat Ptolemy at Cyprus and blockade Egypt.
Demetrius is defeated and falls into Seleucus' power.
Demetrius, sent by Philip, is routed attacking Messene.

Leto.what: Leto has a temple at Argos beside Laphaes' trophy.

Menelaus.what: Menelaus serves as Ptolemy's satrap in Cyprus.
Menelaus pursues Helen with a sword on the chest.

Adrastus.what: Adrastus supplicates Theseus for the Argive dead.
Adrastus, an exile, becomes king of Sicyon.
Adrastus gathers allies, and alone survives the first defeat at Thebes.

Epaminondas.what: Epaminondas is told in a vision to restore the Messenians.
Epaminondas founds the new Messene with sacrifices.
Epaminondas dies and is buried at Mantinea.
Epaminondas wins the battle of Leuctra over Sparta.
Epaminondas founds Megalopolis, defies the term law, and is acquitted.
Epaminondas rescues Pelopidas and is killed at Mantinea.

Pan.what: Pan promises help at Marathon through Philippides.
Pan's temple stands on Mount Lycæus.
Pan reveals Demeter's hiding place on Mount Elaion.

Pausanias.what: Pausanias wins at Platæa and refuses to outrage Mardonius' body.
King Pausanias leaves Athens, is tried, and flees to Tegea.
Pausanias accidentally kills Cleonice and cannot escape the guilt.

Phidias.what: Phidias makes the Nemesis statue at Rhamnus from Persian marble.
Phidias' Zeus at Olympia is described with its throne.
Phidias makes the Marathon statues at Delphi.

Adrian.what: Adrian is honoured as an Eponymus for piety.
Adrian builds the Olympieion and other Athenian buildings.
Adrian rebuilds the temple of Poseidon Hippius.

Amphiaraus.what: Amphiaraus is swallowed by the earth and worshipped at Oropus.
Amphiaraus is shown on the chest, angry at Eriphyle.

Cleomenes.what: Ptolemy kills Cleomenes, the satrap of Egypt.
Cleomenes seizes autocratic power in Sparta, fights the Achaeans, and dies in Egypt.
Cleomenes destroys the Argive army before Telesilla's women.
Cleomenes burns the Argives, bribes the Pythia, and dies mad.

Danaus.what: Danaus wins the Argive kingdom by the wolf omen and builds the temple.
Danaus sets a race for his daughters' suitors.

Helen.what: Helen bears Theseus' child at Argos and dedicates Ilithyia's temple.
Spartan and Rhodian accounts of Helen's end are told.

Antiochus.what: Antiochus, urged by Magas, is checked by Ptolemy.
Antiochus opposes surrender; his party kills Androcles.

Augustus.what: Augustus punishes Messenians who backed Antony.
Augustus resettles Patræ and grants it freedom.
Augustus takes Athene Alea's statue and boar tusks from Tegea.

Cassander.what: Cassander kills Olympias and installs Lachares as tyrant at Athens.
Cassander restores Thebes and kills Alexander's family; his sons destroy one another.

Hygiea.what: Hygiea's statue stands near Silenus' stone.
Hygiea has a statue at Titane's sanctuary.

Leonidas.what: Leonidas holds Thermopylæ with 300 Spartans until betrayed.
Leonidas is deposed, exiled to Arcadia, and recalled.
Leonidas' remains are moved from Thermopylae to Sparta.

Antipater.what: Archias hands exiles to Antipater, but not Demosthenes.
Antipater holds real power in Macedonia after Alexander's death.
Milesian Antipater refuses Dionysius' bribe and keeps his identity.

Aratus.what: Aratus overthrows Nicocles, frees Sicyon, and joins the Achaean league.
Aratus drives Agis out of Pellene.
Aratus' feigned retreat lures Agis to death at Mantinea.

Cadmus.what: Cadmus conquers the land and builds the Cadmea.
Cadmus slays the dragon and sows its teeth.
Cadmus follows a marked cow and founds Thebes.

Dædalus.what: Dædalus works for Minos and flees to Sicily.
Dædalus flees Crete and makes the wooden Hercules at Thebes.

Lycaon.what: Lycaon founds Lycosura, sacrifices a baby, and becomes a wolf.
Lycaon's sons found Arcadian cities and his daughter Callisto is loved by Zeus.

Lysander.what: Lysander helps Agesilaus win the throne and agrees to destroy Athens.
Agias foretells Lysander's victory at Ægos-potamoi.
Samians set up Lysander's statue, showing Ionian flattery.
Lysander is killed at Haliartus and Pausanias assesses his legacy.

Miltiades.what: Miltiades commands the Athenians at Marathon.
Miltiades is tried after failing at Paros and buried at Marathon.
Miltiades is named first benefactor of Greece.

Minos.what: Minos taunts Theseus and throws his ring into the sea.
Minos besieges Nisæa and slays Nisus.
Minos demands tribute after Androgeos' death.
Minos pursues Britomartis, who becomes a goddess.

Œdipus.what: Oedipus' tomb is shown at the Areopagus.
Laius exposes Oedipus, who kills his father and marries his mother.
Oedipus kills his father at the Cross-roads.

Theopompus.what: Theopompus becomes king as Sparta starts hostilities with Messenia.
Theopompus and Euphaes exhort their men before the second campaign's battle.
Theopompus meets Euphaes in battle and is routed by his picked guard.
Theopompus is attacked by Euphaes in the night battle.
Theopompus is slandered by Anaximenes' forged book and turned on by Greece.

Ægeus.what: Ægeus, eldest son of Pandion, becomes king of Athens.
Ægeus throws himself into the sea on seeing black sails.
Ægeus' tokens are retrieved by his son Theseus lifting the stone.

Amphitryon.what: Amphitryon's house and the stories of Hercules' madness are shown at Thebes.

Cronos.what: Cronos is tricked by Rhea at Methydrium and threatens to devour his child.
Cronos is tricked with a stone instead of Zeus on Petrachos.

Hephæstus.what: Hephaestus' temple stands in Athens beside Celestial Aphrodite's cult.
Hephaestus traps Hera in a golden seat.
Hephaestus is named as maker of Agamemnon's sceptre.

Lycurgus.what: Lycurgus gives Sparta its laws and is regent for Labotas.
Lycurgus is honoured as a god with a temple at Sparta.
Lycurgus succeeds Aleus, kills Areithous by guile and outlives his sons.

Lycus.what: Lycus flees from Ægeus and gives the Lyceum its name.
Lycus becomes ruler of Thebes after Nycteus' death.
Lycus arrives from Athens and teaches the mysteries of the Great Goddesses.

Mardonius.what: Mardonius' men lose their way at night and are slain by Megarians.
Mardonius is killed at Platæa and his body spared by Pausanias.
Mardonius' supposed tomb is shown near Hysiæ.

Polynices.what: Polynices and Eteocles kill each other in single combat.
Polynices attacks Thebes with an Argive army.

Agis.what: Agis wars on Elis, fortifies Decelea and doubts his son Leotychides.
Agis takes Pellene but is expelled by Aratus.
Agis is drawn into a crescent by Aratus' feigned retreat and killed.
Agis attacks Megalopolis but his battering-ram is broken by the wind.

Alcamenes.what: Alcamenes settles Crete and destroys Helos.
Alcamenes is father and predecessor of Polydorus.
Alcamenes is sent to Megara with 4,000 men and flees.

Asopus.what: Asopus pays Sisyphus with a fountain for news of Ægina.
Asopus finds the river that bears his name.

Diomede.what: Diomede builds Hippolytus' precincts and first sacrifices to him.
Diomede dedicates the statue of Athene of Winds, ending the gales.

Erechtheus.what: Erechtheus is slain in the war with Eleusis.

Temenus.what: Temenus favours Deiphontes and is killed by his sons.
Temenus is father of Hyrnetho and sons who abduct her.
Temenus rigs the lots with unbaked clay so Cresphontes wins Messenia.

Iphitus.what: Iphitus revives the Olympic games with Delphi's advice.
Iphitus serves as the sole original umpire.
Iphitus is shown crowned by Ecechiria on the temple.

Œnomaus.what: Œnomaus kills Hippodamia's suitors; his tomb and their grave are described.
Œnomaus' son Leucippus disguises himself to win Daphne.

Pindar.what: Pindar dedicates a statue and writes a hymn to Ammon.
Pindar is defeated by Corinna at Thebes.
Pindar is fed by bees, dreams of Proserpine, and is honoured at Thebes.

Priam.what: Priam flees to the altar of Zeus.
Priam is killed by Neoptolemus in the painting of Troy.

Pythian Priestess.what: The Pythian Priestess gives obscure oracles to Aristodemus and the Spartans.
The Priestess prophesies Messene's end when a he-goat drinks from the Neda.
Delphi tells the Phigalians to use 100 men of Oresthasium.
Delphi tells the Orchomenians to fetch Hesiod's bones.
The Priestess advises the Liparaeans to victory.

Agesilaus.what: Agesilaus wins the throne with Lysander's help and a Delphic oracle.
Agesilaus leads the Asian expedition, is attacked at Aulis, and wins at Coronea.
Agesilaus campaigns in Egypt and dies on the voyage home.
Agesilaus questions Epaminondas at Sparta about the peace.

Ajax.what: Ajax is honoured on Salamis; his huge kneecaps are shown.
Ajax fights Hector and drags Cassandra on the chest.
Ajax son of Oileus is shown with Cassandra and the oath.

Archidamus.what: Archidamus ravages Attica and takes Plataea as the Peloponnesian War begins.
Archidamus helps the Phocians at Delphi and dies in Italy.

Eteocles.what: Eteocles kills Polynices and dies in single combat.
Eteocles first sacrifices to the Graces and sets up three.

Ilithyia.what: Ilithyia's temple at Olympia is tied to Sosipolis' worship.
Ilithyia is worshipped at Clitor; Olen equates her with Fate.

Orpheus.what: Orpheus is killed by women; rival accounts of his death and tomb are given.
Orpheus sits in the willow grove with musicians in Polygnotus' painting.

Pirithous.what: Pirithous is imprisoned with Theseus in Thesprotia.
Pirithous' wedding is the setting of the Centaur fight.
Pirithous sits with Theseus on the enchanted rock.

Praxiteles.what: Praxiteles is tricked by Phryne into naming his finest work.

Sisyphus.what: Sisyphus buries Melicerta and founds the Isthmian games.
Sisyphus betrays Ægina's fate to Asopus and gets a fountain.
Sisyphus rolls his stone uphill in the painting.

Tyndareus.what: Tyndareus is exiled by Hippocoon and restored by Hercules.
Tyndareus binds Helen's suitors by oath over the horse.

Alcmena.what: Alcmene dies at Megara and her burial dispute is settled by Apollo.
Alcmena's bridal bed is shown at Thebes.

Cassandra.what: Cassandra is said by some to have thrown the chest away.
Cassandra clings to Athene's statue in the painting.

Alpheus.what: Alpheus loves Arethusa and becomes a river.
Alpheus loves Artemis and is tricked with mud.
The Alpheus repeatedly vanishes underground and reappears at Syracuse.

Amphion.what: Amphion and Zethus seize Thebes and fortify it.
Amphion discovers the lyre chord nete at a gate.
Amphion's music moves stones; he is buried with Zethus.

Atlas.what: Atlas bears Heaven and Earth on the chest of Cypselus.
Atlas is said to meditate at Polus.

Attalus.what: Attalus drives the Galati inland and becomes an Eponymus.
Attalus is the destroyer of the Galati in Phaennis' oracle.

Callisto.what: Callisto is loved by Zeus, turned into a bear and becomes a constellation.
Callisto's tomb is shown in Arcadia.
Callisto is shown in the underworld painting.

Cimon.what: Cimon brings Theseus' bones to Athens.
Cimon's help to Sparta is sent home, leading to the Argive alliance.
Cimon uses the flooding trick at Eion.

Cypselus.what: Cypselus drives out the Bacchidæ and becomes king of Corinth.
Cypselus dedicates a golden statue at Olympia.
Cypselus is hidden in the cedar chest as a child.

Glaucus.what: Glaucus, son of Sisyphus, is father of Bellerophon.
Glaucus of Carystus wins at Olympia after mending a plough by hand.
Glaucus the fisherman becomes a prophetic sea god.

Hippodamia.what: Hippodamia founds the games in thanks to Hera.
Hippodamia is honoured by the women of Elis.
Hippodamia is the prize for which suitors die.

Ino.what: Ino's body is said by Megarians to have washed ashore.
Ino leaps into the sea with Melicerta.
Ino has a dream oracle at Thalamæ.

Iolaus.what: Iolaus has a hero-chapel at Thebes.
Iolaus leads the Thespians and Athenians to Sardinia.

Lynceus.what: Lynceus escapes alone of the fifty brothers and signals from Lyrceia.
Lynceus, keen-sighted son of Aphareus, is described.

Pluto.what: Pluto descends to the underworld near Lerna.
Pluto is honoured only by the Eleans, who open his temple yearly.

Polycletus.what: Polycletus makes the gold and ivory Hera.
Polycletus builds the theatre at Epidaurus.

Polydorus.what: Polydorus, popular and just, is murdered by Polemarchus.
Polydorus is a Lacedaemonian king in the drawn battle.

Seleucus.what: Seleucus flees, returns, defeats Antigonus and is murdered by Ptolemy Lightning.
Seleucus sacrifices at Pella and the altar wood flares up unaided.

Æneas.what: Æneas carries the Palladium to Italy.
Æneas escapes Ilium and is among Sardinia's settlers.

Æpytus.what: Æpytus survives Cresphontes' murder, is restored and punishes the murderers.
Æpytus is killed by a small serpent while hunting.
Æpytus breaks the woollen thread and is blinded by sea water.
Æpytus is buried in a modest tomb on Sepia.

Æschylus.what: Æschylus fights the Persians and is proud of Marathon.
Æschylus is called to write tragedy by Dionysus in a dream.

Agenor.what: Agenor the boxer is bribed by Eupolus.

Antiope.what: Antiope is claimed in war and bears her sons near Eleutheræ.
Antiope goes mad and is cured by Phocus.

Arcas.what: Arcas teaches agriculture and weaving and names Arcadia.
Arcas' bones are moved at Delphi's command and buried at Mantinea.

Arsinoe.what: Arsinoe marries her brother Ptolemy and dies childless.
Arsinoe plots the death of Agathocles, Lysimachus' son.
Arsinoe is claimed by Messenians as Æsculapius' mother.

Cecrops.what: The two Cecrops are untangled in the Athenian royal line.
Cecrops offers only cakes, contrasted with Lycaon's sacrifice.

Cresphontes.what: Cresphontes wins Messenia by lots and is killed by rebels.
Cresphontes reads the oracle of the three-eyed leader.

Hesiod.what: Hesiod's works and death are disputed at Hippocrene.
Hesiod's bones are brought from Naupactus to Orchomenus.

Lacedaemonians.what: The Lacedaemonians fight the Messenians to a drawn battle.
The Spartans try deception with fake deserters and clay tripods.
The Spartans raze Ithome and impose harsh terms on the Messenians.

Nero.what: Nero grants Greece its freedom; Vespasian later withdraws it.
Nero carries off five hundred bronze statues from Delphi.

Phoroneus.what: Phoroneus gathers men into communities as the first mortal in the land.
The Argives credit Phoroneus with inventing fire.

Pisistratus.what: Pisistratus builds the spring called the Nine Springs.

Rhea.what: Rhea hides her son Poseidon among the lambs.
Rhea hides the infant Zeus from Cronos by giving him a stone.
Rhea deceives Cronos with a stone.

Telephus.what: Telephus, son of Auge, is exposed on Mount Parthenium.
Telephus is exposed as a boy and nursed by a doe.

Tiresias.what: Tiresias cuts off the serpent's head.
Tiresias dies after drinking from the spring Tilphusa.

Trophonius.what: Trophonius bids a trophy be made from Aristomenes' shield before Leuctra.
Trophonius robs the treasury with Agamedes, beheads him, and is swallowed by the earth at Lebadea.
Trophonius' oracle at Lebadea is consulted by those who descend into the cave.
Trophonius teaches Saon the rites after the bees reveal the oracle.

Æacus.what: Æacus prays for rain on Ægina to end the drought.

Ægialeus.what: Ægialeus is the first king of Sicyon.
Ægialeus, son of Adrastus, leads an expedition against Thebes.

Ariadne.what: Ariadne's ashes are said to be buried at Argos.

Conon.what: Conon builds a temple of Aphrodite at the Piraeus.
Conon wins the sea-fight at Cnidus and is honoured by the Ionians.

Eros.what: Eros is worshipped as chief god of the Thespians.

Medusa.what: Medusa's head is said to lie in a mound at Argos.
Medusa's lock of hair protects Tegea.

Sun.what: The Sun disputes Corinth with Poseidon and yields the Isthmus.
The Sun receives Acro-Corinthus and yields it to Aphrodite.

Lycortas.what: Lycortas defends the Achæans before Appius but is jeered.
Lycortas marches on Messene, executes the culprits and avenges Philopoemen.

Lysimachus.what: Lysimachus allies with Ptolemy against Antigonus.
Lysimachus is defeated by the Getae, then founds a new Ephesus.
Lysimachus wins Macedonia, kills his son Agathocles through Arsinoe, and dies fighting Seleucus.

Machaon.what: Machaon is honoured with a shrine and tomb at Gerenia.

Messenians.what: The Messenians fortify Ithome and Aristodemus sacrifices his daughter.
Conquered Messenians suffer Spartan terms and plan revolt under Aristomenes.
Messenian refugees are received by the Arcadians on Lycæus.
The Messenians seize Œniadæ and escape the Acarnanians by night.
The Messenians seize Elis with Spartan-marked shields.

Neleus.what: Neleus settles at Pylos after being received by Aphareus.
Neleus drives out Pylos and makes the city renowned.

Nestor.what: Nestor's house and tomb are shown at Pylos.

Pandion.what: Pandion is exiled to Megara and dies there.
Pandion has a hero-chapel at Megara.

Philopoemen.what: Philopoemen saves Megalopolis from Cleomenes, fights at Sellasia and wins at the Larisus.
Philopoemen reforms the infantry and kills Machanidas at Mantinea.
Philopoemen brings Sparta into the League, is captured by the Messenians and poisoned.
Philopoemen is declared the last benefactor of Greece.

Phocus.what: Phocus is killed by Peleus with a quoit.
Phocus, son of Ornytion, cures Antiope and shares her tomb.

Tantalus.what: Tantalus is shown punished beneath the winejar in the underworld painting.

Themistocles.what: Themistocles makes the Piraeus the port of Athens.
Themistocles wins the victory at Salamis.
Themistocles brings Persian spoils to Delphi, but the Priestess refuses them.

Thersander.what: Thersander is killed by Telephus in Mysia.
Thersander leads the Epigoni against Thebes.

Timotheus.what: Timotheus the Milesian harpist is censured by the Spartans.

Tisamenus.what: Tisamenus is driven out of Argos by the Heraclidae.
Tisamenus the seer wins five victories for Sparta.

Aleus.what: Aleus becomes king and builds the temple at Tegea.
Aleus builds the old temple of Athene Alea.

Augeas.what: Augeas refuses Hercules his reward for cleaning the dung.
Augeas fights Hercules, who kills the sons of Actor.

Codrus.what: Codrus' sons Medon and Nileus quarrel over the kingship.
Codrus devotes himself to death for Athens.

Darius.what: Darius receives the exiled Demaratus in Persia.

Eurydice.what: Eurydice is the wife of Orpheus.

Eurystheus.what: Eurystheus pursues the children of Hercules.
Eurystheus flees Attica and is killed by Iolaus.

Hermione.what: Hermione, Helen's daughter, is wife of Pyrrhus then Orestes.

Hyllus.what: Hyllus is killed by Echemus in single combat.

Ion.what: Ion commands the Athenians against Eleusis.
Ion marries Helice, inherits the kingdom and renames the people Ionians.

Lelex.what: Lelex comes from Egypt as an early king of Megara.
Lelex rules Laconia as its first autochthonous king.

Melampus.what: Melampus cures the women of Argos.
Melampus cures the mad daughters of Proetus at Lusi.

Niobe.what: Niobe, mourning, is turned to rock on Sipylus.

Œneus.what: Œneus is expelled from Aetolia and buried at Oenoe.

Olympias.what: Olympias is besieged and killed by Cassander.
Olympias kills Cleopatra's baby and Aridæus.

Oxylus.what: Oxylus, the muleteer, guides the Dorians and is promised Elis.
Oxylus wins Elis by the single combat of Pyræchmes and Degmenus.
Oxylus' spies enter Elis in silence.

Pelasgus.what: Pelasgus, first king, teaches huts, pigskin clothing and acorns.

Semele.what: Semele and infant Dionysus wash ashore at Brasiae in a chest.
Semele is struck by lightning in her bridal chamber.

Sulla.what: Sulla captures Athens and later suffers a disease as punishment.
Sulla punishes Thebes for joining Mithridates.
Sulla removes the ivory statue at Alalcomenae.

Telamon.what: Telamon rules Salamis and watches his sons sail.
Telamon, exiled for Phocus' death, sails back to Salamis.

Thrasybulus.what: Thrasybulus the Elean seer has a statue at Olympia.
Thrasybulus the Elean seer prophesies victory.

Xenophon.what: Xenophon lives in exile at Scillus and builds a temple to Artemis.

Actæon.what: Actaeon is killed by his dogs, with Pausanias disputing Stesichorus' version.
Actaeon's spectre harms Orchomenus until Delphi orders his remains buried and a bronze copy fastened.

Agamedes.what: Agamedes builds the treasury of Hyrieus with Trophonius, robs it and is trapped and beheaded.
Agamedes and Trophonius build the stone temple of Apollo at Delphi.

Amphictyon.what: Amphictyon takes the Athenian throne after Cranaus and is ousted by Erichthonius.

Anaxander.what: Under King Anaxander the Messenians revolt, are defeated and leave or become slaves.
Anaxander's division is routed by Aristomenes, and he pursues him at Pharae.

Androcles.what: Androcles urges surrendering Polychares and is killed by Antiochus' party.

Aphareus.what: Aphareus rules Messenia, builds Arene and receives Neleus and Lycus.

Aristo.what: Aristo doubts his son Demaratus because of the early birth.

Athamas.what: Athamas leads Minyae from Orchomenus to settle Teos.
Athamas receives land from Andreus, and the golden ram saves his children.

Bellerophon.what: Bellerophon is discussed with the temple of Athene the Bridler and Corinth's kings.

Brennus.what: Brennus persuades the Galati to invade Greece and musters a huge army.
Brennus bridges the Sperchius and attacks the Greeks at Thermopylae, repulsed.
Brennus crosses Oeta in mist, routs the Phocians and forces the Greeks to evacuate.
Brennus is wounded at Delphi, retreats and kills himself.

Earth.what: Earth is the earliest holder of the Delphic oracle.
Earth sets the dragon to guard her oracle at Pytho.

Callias.what: Callias wins the pancratium at night at Olympia.
Callias dedicates a horse at Delphi from Persian war profits.

Callippus.what: Callippus leads the Athenians holding Thermopylae against the Celts until outflanked.
Callippus bribes his rivals and is fined for a Zanes statue.

Cepheus.what: Cepheus receives from Athene a lock of Medusa to protect Tegea.

Cleombrotus.what: Cleombrotus falls at Leuctra; the later Cleombrotus helps depose Leonidas.
Cleombrotus invades, loses at Leuctra and falls.

Cleon.what: Cleon the Magnesian tells of seeing a huge sea monster.

Damophon.what: Damophon's statues adorn Messene's market-place and Asklepieion.
The tyrant Damophon wrongs Elis and sixteen cities arbitrate.
Damophon makes the single-block statues of Despoena and Demeter.

Deucalion.what: Deucalion's flood destroys Parnassus' town; survivors follow wolves to found Lycorea.

Elatus.what: Elatea claims descent from Arcadian founder Elatus.

Eriphyle.what: Eriphyle is killed by her son Alcmæon, who goes mad.

Eumolpus.what: Eumolpus fights Athens, and the Eleusinian priests descend from him.
Eumolpus stays at Eleusis after arbitration ends the war.

Gelon.what: Gelon of Gela dedicates a chariot at Olympia.
Gelon leads 300 picked Phocians killed by Thessalians.

Hippocoon.what: Hippocoon's sons refuse to cleanse Hercules and are killed by him.

Hypermnestra.what: Hypermnestra disobeys Danaus and spares her husband.
Hypermnestra and Lynceus agree to signal his escape with torches.

Iphigenia.what: Iphigenia lands at Brauron with the statue of Artemis from the Tauri.
Iphigenia accompanies Orestes with the Tauric statue to Sparta.
Iphigenia is to be sacrificed at Aulis but a doe replaces her.

Jason.what: Jason, husband of Medea, rules Corinth, with rival accounts of his fate.
Jason is shown wooing Medea on the Chest of Cypselus.

Leotychides.what: Leotychides replaces Demaratus, fights at Mycale, takes bribes and flees to Tegea.
Agis doubts Leotychides' legitimacy, and Agesilaus takes the throne.

Leucippus.what: Leucippus disguises himself as a girl to win Daphne and is killed.

Melanthus.what: Melanthus becomes king at Athens after the Heraclidae return.

Meleager.what: Meleager's death is the matter of the wood Callipolis throws down.
Meleager appears in the painting, with his death by the firebrand told.

Melicerta.what: Ino leaps into the sea with Melicerta, who becomes Palæmon.
Melicerta is carried by a dolphin and honoured at the Isthmus.
Melicerta is buried in a crypt in the temple of Palæmon.

Menestheus.what: Menestheus succeeds Theseus as king of Athens.
Menestheus is restored to power in Athens while Theseus is away.

Metellus.what: Metellus asks the Achæans to treat Sparta kindly and reports unfavourably in Rome.
Metellus, busy with Andriscus, has envoys forbid the Achaean war on Sparta.
Metellus offers peace, defeats Critolaus at Scarphea and enters Thebes.

Mummius.what: Mummius dedicates bronze Zeus statues from Achaean spoils.
Mummius is chosen consul and sent against the Achaeans.
Mummius defeats the Achaeans at the Isthmus, then sacks and burns Corinth.

Onatas.what: Onatas makes the bronze Black Demeter statue for the Phigalians.

Patroclus.what: Patroclus fortifies an island off Sunium for Egypt.
Patroclus asks the Spartans to engage Antigonus besieging Athens.

Pegasus.what: Pegasus' hoof raises a spring at Troezen.

Peleus.what: Peleus kills his half-brother Phocus with a quoit.
Peleus seizes Thetis on the Chest of Cypselus.

Perieres.what: Perieres, son of Æolus, rules Messenia.

Philoctetes.what: Philoctetes' bow of Hercules is sent for, as Troy cannot fall without it.
Philoctetes is left on Lemnos with an ulcer.

Phormio.what: Phormio, a debtor, is made Athenian admiral.
Phormio refuses Castor and Pollux the girl's chamber, and she vanishes.
Blind fisherman Phormio dreams of the hair rope and is healed.

Polygnotus.what: Polygnotus paints Antenor's house spared at Troy.
Polygnotus paints the Underworld at Delphi.

Procles.what: Procles and his twin Eurysthenes found two royal houses of Sparta.
Procles leads Epidaurian Ionians to Samos.

Prœtus.what: Proetus rules Tiryns and the coast after the kingdom is divided.
Proetus fights a drawn battle with Acrisius.

Prometheus.what: Prometheus has an altar at the Academy, starting point of the torch race.

Protesilaus.what: Protesilaus is honoured as a hero at Eleus.

Pythagoras.what: Pythagoras the Wise is great-grandson of Hippasus.

Sthenelus.what: Sthenelus takes the three-eyed Zeus statue as spoil.

Teleclus.what: Teleclus is killed by the Messenians.
King Teleclus is killed at the temple of Artemis Limnas.

Theagenes.what: Theagenes outboxes Euthymus at Olympia, is fined, then gives up boxing.
Theagenes' boyhood feat, 1400 crowns, and his statue's fall and cult.

Thetis.what: Thetis is seized by Peleus on the chest.
Thetis pleads for her son in the Apollonian group.

Timon.what: Timon the misanthrope has a tower near Athens.

Tyrtæus.what: Tyrtaeus is quoted on Messenian servitude.
Tyrtæus, the lame Athenian schoolmaster, is sent to Sparta and recites his verses.
Tyrtæus rallies the Spartans after Aristomenes' charge.

Xanthippus.what: Xanthippus, son of Deiphontes, is part of the Hyrnetho story.

Æthra.what: Æthra crosses to the island after Athene's dream and lies with Poseidon.
Æthra, wife of Phalanthus, weeps on his head, fulfilling the oracle of rain from a clear sky.

Agesipolis.what: Agesipolis invades Argolis despite earthquakes and later dies of disease at Olynthus.
Agesipolis captures Mantinea by flooding its brick walls with the river.

Alcathous.what: Alcathous kills the lion of Cithaeron and becomes king of Megara.
Alcathous accidentally kills his son Callipolis with a piece of wood at the altar.

Alcmæon.what: Alcmæon, mad after killing his mother, marries Alphesibœa and Callirhoe and is killed by Phegeus' sons.

Amphitrite.what: Amphitrite gives Theseus a golden crown when he dives for Minos' ring.

Arcadians.what: The Arcadians refuse Sparta's deception and capture Lyciscus, bringing him to Ithome.
The Arcadians shelter Messenian refugees and stone the traitor Aristocrates.

Areus.what: Areus leads the Spartan army toward Athens against Antigonus but turns home for lack of supplies.

Boreas.what: Boreas is shown carrying off Orithyia, with serpent tails for feet.

Capaneus.what: Capaneus is struck by lightning at the walls of Thebes.

Charillus.what: Charillus is ambushed and captured by the Tegean women.

Cleonnis.what: Cleonnis commands the heavy-armed troops that hold against the Spartans at Ithome.

Cleonymus.what: Cleonymus, denied the kingdom, brings Pyrrhus against Sparta.
Cleonymus, passed over for the kingship, becomes an enemy and invites Pyrrhus against Sparta.

Clisthenes.what: Clisthenes of Sicyon leads the Amphictyones against Cirrha.

Clymenus.what: Clymenus inherits the kingdom of Orchomenus and is killed by Thebans.

Damaretus.what: Damaretus of Heraea is first winner of the armed race at Olympia.

Demaratus.what: Demaratus is deposed after Cleomenes bribes the Delphic priestess.
Demaratus loses his kingdom and goes to Darius in Persia.

Diaeus.what: Diæus, bribed, saves Menalcidas and lies to the Achæans about the Senate's ruling.
Diaeus frees slaves to raise an army and spoils Metellus's peace offer.
Diaeus flees to Megalopolis, kills his wife and poisons himself.

Dorieus.what: Dorieus wins pancratium crowns, goes into exile, and is executed by Sparta.

Echemus.what: Echemus becomes king of the Arcadians and kills Hyllus in single combat.

Epeus.what: Epeus wins the kingdom of Elis in a race against his brothers.

Euphaes.what: Euphaes drills the Messenians and holds a fortified camp against Sparta.
Euphaes routs Theopompus's wing in a night-ended draw.
Euphaes persuades the people that Aristodemus's sacrifice fulfilled the oracle.
Euphaes is mortally wounded in battle and dies after thirteen years as king.

Eurypylus.what: Eurypylus, driven mad by Dionysus's statue, is cured at Aroe and ends the sacrifices.

Gorgus.what: Gorgus, son of Aristomenes, marries the maiden who freed his father.
Gorgus proposes Zacynthus and helps capture Zancle, renamed Messene.

Gryllus.what: Gryllus is said to have mortally wounded Epaminondas at Mantinea.
Gryllus is named as the killer of Epaminondas.

Hippolytus.what: Hippolytus dies through his father's curses after Phaedra's accusation.
Hippolytus is revived by Æsculapius and becomes king at Aricia.
Hippolytus is honoured with a Trœzen precinct; his chariot overturns at the olive tree.

Laodamas.what: Laodamas flees with Theban exiles after the defeat at Glisas.

Nabis.what: Nabis, the cruel ruler of Sparta, falls and the Achaeans take Sparta.
Nabis takes Messene, is attacked by Philopoemen and is assassinated by an Aetolian-hired man.

Nisus.what: Nisus, king of Megara, loses his purple lock to his daughter during Minos's siege.

Œbalus.what: Œbalus tricks the Messenians with clay tripods at Ithome.

Pelias.what: Pelias is tricked by Medea and boiled by his own daughters.

Philomelus.what: Philomelus urges the Phocians to seize Delphi and dies at Neon.

Polybius.what: Polybius's statue stands in Megalopolis, and Pausanias praises his history.

Promachus.what: Promachus of Pellene is honoured with a statue as pancratium victor.

Pylades.what: Pylades sings of freedom for Hellas at the Nemean games.

Scopas.what: Scopas builds the large temple of Athene Alea at Tegea.

Thamyris.what: Thamyris is blinded at Dorium and throws away his lyre, giving the river Balyra its name
Thamyris sits blind and dejected with his broken lyre among the musicians in Polygnotus' painting

Theodorus.what: Theodorus the Samian builds the Scias at Sparta
Theodorus is discussed as an early bronze caster and emerald seal maker
Theodorus the Samian brass-founder is named as maker of a work at Amphissa

Triptolemus.what: Triptolemus is the subject of rival Argive and Athenian stories about his parentage and sowing of corn
Triptolemus helps found Aroe and Anthea in early Patræ
Triptolemus teaches Arcas how to sow corn

Zethus.what: Zethus is born to Antiope near Eleutheræ with his twin Amphion
Zethus and Amphion seize Thebes and fortify it
Zethus is buried with Amphion in a mound whose earth is disputed

Acrisius.what: Acrisius is accidentally killed by Perseus' quoit, fulfilling the oracle
Acrisius builds the brazen chamber for his daughter
Acrisius fights a drawn battle with his rival Proetus

Acrotatus.what: Acrotatus, father of Areus, succeeds in the Spartan royal line
Acrotatus is beaten and killed fighting Megalopolis under Aristodemus

Ægina.what: Ægina is carried off by Zeus, a story told through Asopus' fountain
Ægina gives her name to the island whose history is traced

Alcibiades.what: Alcibiades is courted by the Ionians as the man in power
Alcibiades joins Areus in accusing the Achæans before Rome

Arcesilaus.what: Arcesilaus the Spartan horse-breeder has a statue; his son Lichas is scourged
Arcesilaus is said to have seen the very old collared stag

Arethusa.what: Arethusa flees Alpheus to Ortygia and becomes a spring
Arethusa's spring at Syracuse is where the Alpheus is said to reappear

Aristæus.what: Aristæus leads Greeks to Sardinia after Sardus

Aristocrates.what: Aristocrates takes Spartan bribes and leads the Arcadians in flight at the Great Trench
Aristocrates betrays Aristomenes' plan, is exposed by a letter and stoned
Aristocrates violates Artemis' priestess and is stoned; his grandson is stoned too

Aristogiton.what: Aristogiton is honoured with a statue as Hipparchus' killer

Asterion.what: Asterion the river judges for Hera in her dispute with Poseidon

Atalanta.what: Atalanta is said to have made water gush from a rock
Atalanta is the first to hit the Calydonian boar

Atreus.what: Atreus kills Thyestes' children in their feud

Auge.what: Auge bears Hercules' child, is set adrift in a chest and marries Teuthras
Auge gives birth on her knees; her statue stands at Ilithyia's temple

Azan.what: Azan receives a share of Arcadia from his father Arcas

Bacis.what: Bacis' oracles encourage Epaminondas to refound Messene
Bacis' oracle explains the Tithorean earth-taking custom

Bias.what: Bias shares the kingdom of Argos with his brother Melampus

Callicrates.what: Callicrates denounces Achaeans to a Roman senator, sending over 1,000 to Italy
Callicrates takes Oropian bribes and helps split the Achaean League
Callicrates prosecutes Menalcidas for cheating him and dies on the road

Callon.what: Callon of Elis makes bronze images of the drowned Messenian chorus

Canachus.what: Canachus the Sicyonian makes the statue of Aphrodite

Carmanor.what: Carmanor purifies Apollo of the killing of Python

Caucon.what: Caucon brings the mysteries of the Great Goddesses from Eleusis
Caucon appears in dreams guiding the return of the Messenians

Celeus.what: Celeus' daughters perform the Eleusinian rites in the war story
Celeus is cited among Eleusinians taught the mysteries by Demeter

Galati.what: The Galati invade Macedonia and Greece, are repulsed at Delphi, and settle in Galatia
Gallic mercenaries plot against Ptolemy and perish on a desert island
The Galati under Brennus cross the Sperchius, forcing the Greeks to withdraw
The Galati attack Thermopylae furiously and are driven back with heavy losses

Chloris.what: Chloris, Niobe's daughter, turns pale from fear
Chloris wins the first footrace at Hippodamia's games

Cisus.what: Cisus, Temenus' eldest son, becomes king of Argos
Cisus is among Temenus' sons who seek to take Hyrnetho

Cleopatra.what: Cleopatra favours her younger son Alexander and has Philometor exiled
Cleopatra's baby boy by Philip is killed by Olympias

Clytæmnestra.what: Clytæmnestra is buried outside the walls of Mycenae
Clytæmnestra raises Helen's child at Argos

Corœbus.what: Corœbus kills the monster Punishment, goes to Delphi and is buried at Megara
Corœbus wins the first footrace after the revival of the games

Coronis.what: Coronis is the mother of Æsculapius in the Epidaurian tradition

Craugis.what: Craugis is named as Philopoemen's noble father

Creon.what: Creon refuses burial to the Argive dead after the Theban war

Crotopus.what: Crotopus' tomb is shown at Argos

Cylon.what: Cylon the Olympic victor plots to rule Athens
Cylon kills the tyrant Aristotimus at the altar of Zeus Soter

Cynisca.what: Cynisca becomes the first woman to win at Olympia
Cynisca dedicates bronze horses at Olympia
Cynisca's chariot group stands at Olympia

Cyrus.what: Cyrus funds the Spartan fleet through Lysander

Deiphontes.what: Deiphontes is favoured by Temenus as general and son-in-law
Deiphontes takes Epidauria with the Argives
Deiphontes kills Cerynes defending his wife Hyrnetho

Demosthenes.what: Demosthenes is exiled twice and dies by poison on Calauria
Pausanias clears Demosthenes of taking Harpalus' money

Endymion.what: Endymion rules Elis, and his sons race for the kingdom
Endymion deposes Clymenus and holds games at Olympia

Ephialtes.what: Ephialtes the giant is buried at Anthedon with his brother Otus
Ephialtes and Otus are said to have first sacrificed to the Muses

Epimenides.what: Epimenides the Gnossian is said to have slept forty years
Epimenides builds the round building at Sparta

Epopeus.what: Epopeus takes Antiope and fights Thebes, dying of his wounds

Eurytus.what: Eurytus is shot by Hercules and has a tomb at Cleonæ

Evagoras.what: Evagoras of Cyprus has a statue near the royal portico
Evagoras of Elis wins the pair-horse race

Fortune.what: Fortune is discussed as a powerful daughter of Oceanus with a temple at Pharae
Fortune has a temple at Elis

Hebe.what: Hebe is worshipped at Phlius in a grove temple

Geryon.what: Geryon's famed oxen are cited among ancient cattle legends

Helenus.what: Helenus guides Pyrrhus to Epirus and marries Andromache
Argive claims to Helenus' tomb are rejected

Hellanicus.what: Hellanicus conspires against the tyrant Aristotimus

Herodes.what: Herodes builds the white marble stadium at Athens
Herodes adorns the Delphi stadium with Pentelican marble

Hippocrates.what: Hippocrates is attacked by Dinomenes in the Syracusan story
Hippocrates, Athenian general, is killed at Delium

Hyrnetho.what: Hyrnetho is Temenus' favourite daughter, married to Deiphontes
Hyrnetho is accidentally killed by her brother Phalces

Icarius.what: Icarius proposes a race for Penelope's suitors
Icarius pleads with Penelope to stay and sets up a statue of Modesty

Lacedaemon.what: Lacedaemon names the country and Sparta after himself

Leosthenes.what: Leosthenes leads the Athenian revolt against Macedon after Alexander's death and dies.

Lycomedes.what: Lycomedes plots Theseus' death on Scyrus, where Theseus is killed.

Manto.what: Manto, a Theban captive, marries Rhacius at Claros and bears Mopsus.
Manto is sent by Apollo to Colophon after Tiresias dies.

Marpessa.what: Marpessa leads the Tegean women in the ambush that captures Charillus.

Medea.what: Medea's flight, rule at Corinth and her children's fate are told in rival versions.
Medea tricks Pelias' daughters into boiling their father.

Melanippus.what: Melanippus and Comaetho couple in Artemis's temple, bringing famine, plague and annual sacrifices.

Menalcidas.what: Menalcidas keeps the Oropian bribe, is prosecuted by Callicrates, and is saved by Diæus.
Menalcidas breaks the truce by sacking Iasus, then poisons himself.

Messene.what: Messene marries Polycaon and gives her name to the land.

Myron.what: Myron, historian of Priene, is criticised by Pausanias for inaccuracy about Aristomenes.
Myron, king of Sicyon, builds the Sicyonian treasury at Olympia.

Myrtilus.what: Myrtilus betrays Œnomaus and is killed by Pelops; Pheneus keeps his tomb.

Olympiodorus.what: Olympiodorus leads old men and boys to expel the Macedonians and take the Museum.

Patreus.what: Patreus enlarges Aroe and names it Patræ.

Phædra.what: Phædra loves Hippolytus, according to the Troezenian story.
Phædra's myrtle and tomb mark her love for Hippolytus at Trœzen.

Phalces.what: Phalces accidentally kills Hyrnetho while trying to carry her off from Deiphontes.

Polycaon.what: Polycaon marries Messene, invades the country and names it Messene.

Polydamas.what: Polydamas performs his feats, kills Immortals at Susa, and dies holding up a collapsing cave.

Preugenes.what: Preugenes brings Artemis Limnatis from Sparta to Patræ.

Procne.what: Procne and Philomela are transformed into birds after Tereus' crime.

Solon.what: Solon rouses Athens to retake Salamis from Megara.
Solon advises the Amphictyones; his hellebore trick helps capture Cirrha.

Teucer.what: Teucer defends himself before his father Telamon in the Athenian law-courts.

Theras.what: Theras, with the twin kings, colonizes Calliste, renamed Thera.
Theras objects for Aristodemus's sons when Cresphontes claims Messenia.

Xuthus.what: Xuthus, exiled, goes to Athens then Ægialus, where his son Ion marries Helice.

Sostratus.what: Sostratus, youth of Dyme loved by Hercules, has his tomb there.

Aeropus.what: Aeropus, an infant, nurses from his dying mother Aerope, fathered by Ares.

Agathocles.what: Agathocles is put to death after Arsinoe plots against him.

Alexanor.what: Alexanor founds the temple of Æsculapius at Titane and is honoured as a hero.

Amyclas.what: Amyclas founds Amyclae and his son Hyacinthus dies.

Anaxandrides.what: Anaxandrides defeats Tegea when Lichas finds Orestes' bones, and takes a second wife.

Ancæus.what: Ancæus dies, killed by the boar, while his father Lycurgus outlives him.

Andromache.what: Andromache appears among the captive Trojan women in Polygnotus' painting.

Antander.what: Antander commands Messenian cavalry and light troops at the ravine and in the second campaign.
Antander is killed defending the wounded King Euphaes.

Antenor.what: Antenor's family leaves his house, spared by the Greeks, in Polygnotus' painting.

Antinoe.what: Antinoe moves the town of Mantinea, guided by a serpent.
Antinoe, a daughter of Pelias, is tricked by Medea into boiling her father.

Archias.what: Archias hands exiles to Antipater but not Demosthenes.

Arion.what: The horse Arion is borne by Demeter to Poseidon.

Callimachus.what: Callimachus the Polemarch is shown at the battle of Marathon.

Caprus.what: Caprus wins wrestling and pancratium on one day, beating Clitomachus.

Cercyon.what: Cercyon kills Alope and the wrestlers he meets until Theseus defeats him.

Chilon.what: Chilon joins the four men who depose the tyrant Aristotimus.

Clinias.what: Clinias' son Aratus overthrows the tyrant Nicocles.

Critolaus.what: Critolaus, as General, deceives the Roman commissioners and raises an army for war.
Critolaus rejects Metellus' peace, is beaten at Scarphea and vanishes.

Crius.what: Crius' insolent son plunders the Delphic temple and is foretold punishment.

Cycnus.what: Cycnus' son Tennes cuts his father's ship ropes with an axe.

Damis.what: Damis competes for the kingship but Aristodemus is chosen.
Damis is appointed dictator and the Messenians leave Ithome.

Despœna.what: Despoena's sanctuary is described with Damophon's statues and rites.
Despoena is named as Demeter's daughter by Poseidon.

Diagoras.what: Diagoras is carried on his sons' shoulders amid flowers.

Dysaules.what: Dysaules is said to found Celeae's rites after being driven from Eleusis.

Epochus.what: Epochus dies of illness while his father Lycurgus survives him.

Erato.what: Erato bears Arcas three legitimate sons.
Erato interprets Pan's oracles at his temple.

Eumenides.what: The Eumenides' temple at Cerynea drives the guilty mad.
The Eumenides pursue Orestes, worshipped at Maniæ.

Erysichthon.what: Erysichthon dies returning from Delos and is buried at Prasiae.

Eryx.what: Eryx the wrestler is killed by Hercules.

Eutelidas.what: Eutelidas wins the boys' wrestling and pentathlum at Olympia.

Flaminius.what: Flaminius besieges Corinth and defeats Philip at Cynoscephalae.

Hagno.what: Hagno nursed Zeus and gave her name to a spring.

Hippias.what: Hippias tortures Leæna to death after the plot against the tyrants.

Hippothoon.what: Hippothoon is born to Alope and Poseidon, his mother put to death by Cercyon.

Hyacinthus.what: Hyacinthus, youngest handsome son of Amyclas, dies young.
Hyacinthus is buried at Amyclae and honoured with an altar beside Apollo's statue.

Immaradus.what: Immaradus, son of Eumolpus, is slain in the war between Eleusis and Athens.

Iphicrates.what: Iphicrates attacks Epaminondas near Lechæum and is routed.

Laius.what: Laius is warned by Delphi, exposes Oedipus and is killed by him.
Laius is killed by Œdipus at the Cross-roads and buried there.

Laphaes.what: Laphaes, Argive king, is expelled and slain, and receives a trophy.

Lyciscus.what: Lyciscus's supposed daughter is drawn by lot; he flees to Sparta when exposed.
Lyciscus is accused of treason and cleared by the priestess of Hera.

Lysandra.what: Lysandra flees to Seleucus with her children and kin after Agathocles' death.

Lysistratus.what: Lysistratus, Corinthian leader, is killed in Aristomenes' night attack.

Melas.what: Athene takes the form of Melas, and Teuthis stabs her at Aulis.

Micon.what: Micon paints the Amazon war and other pictures in Theseus' temple.

Minyas.what: Minyas builds the first Treasury at Orchomenus.

Mithridates.what: Mithridates fights Rome, and Sulla takes Athens in the war.
Thebes joins Mithridates against Rome and is punished by Sulla.

Nauplius.what: Nauplius is ordered to drown Auge.

Nemesis.what: Nemesis is honoured at Rhamnus in Phidias' statue with its base.

Nicocles.what: Nicocles, tyrant of Sicyon, is attacked by night and driven out by Aratus.

Ophioneus.what: Ophioneus goes blind again, understands the oracle and kills himself at her grave.

Penelope.what: Penelope veils her face when Icarius pleads with her to stay in Lacedaemon.

Phalanthus.what: Phalanthus is told to found a city where rain falls from a clear sky; takes Tarentum.

Philomela.what: Philomela, wronged by Tereus, is turned into a bird.
Philomela becomes a bird, fearing Tereus.

Phintas.what: In Phintas' reign the Messenians first send a choir to Delos.

Phlegyas.what: Phlegyas renames the country and city; his people attack Delphi and are defeated.

Phryne.what: Phryne tricks Praxiteles into naming his finest work.

Pirene.what: Pirene becomes a well, weeping for her son.

Pisander.what: Pisander gives the Hydra many heads, which Pausanias doubts.
Pisander is appointed fleet commander by Agesilaus after the victory near Sardis.

Platæa.what: Platæa is honoured with a chapel in the town.

Plistarchus.what: Plistarchus, a young child, is represented by regent Pausanias after Platæa.

Procris.what: Procris is shown among the women in the underworld painting, murdered by Cephalus.

Prytanis.what: Prytanis, a Cyzicene boxer, is bribed by Eupolus.

Sleep.what: A statue of Sleep lulls a lion in Æsculapius' precinct.
Sleep is shown as a white child held by Night.

Stesichorus.what: Stesichorus, blinded for slandering Helen, receives her message through Leonymus.

Stymphelus.what: Stymphelus, founder of the town, is the namesake of its Hera temples' city.

Telesilla.what: Telesilla arms slaves and women to defend Argos against Cleomenes.

Tereus.what: Tereus kills himself at Megara and receives annual sacrifices.
Tereus is changed into a hoopoe after eating his son.

Teuthras.what: Teuthras marries Auge after her chest drifts to Mysia.

Thebans.what: The Thebans fight the Phocians for ten years in the Sacred War.

Themis.what: Themis receives the Delphic oracle from Earth.

Theoclus.what: Theoclus interprets the he-goat oracle as a wild fig tree.
Theoclus rallies the Messenians at Eira, declares the fall fated, and dies fighting.

Thestius.what: Thestius' fifty daughters are given to Hercules, explaining his virgin priestess.

Tityus.what: Tityus is shown worn to a shadow in the underworld painting.

Xenias.what: Xenias plots for Sparta in Elis, but the plot fails.

Achaeans.what: The Achaeans form their League at Aegium and fight Sparta.
The Achaeans march on Sparta under Damocritus and win a battle.

Æacides.what: Æacides fights with Olympias against Cassander's side and dies.

Aethlius.what: Aethlius is the first king of Elis.

Aetolus.what: Aetolus flees Elis after accidentally killing Apis.

Agapenor.what: Agapenor leads the Arcadians to Troy and founds Paphos in Cyprus.

Alcis.what: Alcis dies with her sister to win the war against Orchomenus.

Aletes.what: Aletes takes Corinth as Dorian leader.

Alope.what: Alope bears Hippothoon to Poseidon and is put to death by Cercyon.

Anaxilas.what: Anaxilas invites the Messenians to Rhegium and carries them over to Sicily.

Andræmon.what: Andræmon drives the Carians out of Lebedus.

Andreus.what: Andreus becomes first settler of Orchomenus.

Androclus.what: Androclus takes Ephesus and dies fighting for Priene
Androclus and the Ephesians expel Leogorus's Samians from Samos

Androgeos.what: Androgeos is killed by the bull, leading to Minos' tribute demand

Anteros.what: Anteros avenges Timagoras and is worshipped by resident aliens

Antonine.what: Antonine builds in the sanctuary of Aesculapius at Epidaurus
Antonine favours Pallantium, wages wars, relieves disasters and gives generous laws

Apis.what: Apis is accidentally killed by Aetolus' chariot, so Aetolus flees

Aras.what: Aras founds Arantia as first inhabitant of Phliasia

Archelaus.what: Archelaus enslaves Ægys and destroys Amyclæ, Pharis and Geranthræ

Areithous.what: Areithous is killed by Lycurgus through guile

Argeus.what: Argeus is son of Deiphontes, named in the Hyrnetho story

Arimnestus.what: Arimnestus, king of the Tyrrhenians, dedicates a throne to Olympian Zeus

Aristotimus.what: Aristotimus seizes power in Elis and is killed by Cylon at the altar

Britomartis.what: Britomartis flees Minos and becomes a goddess, Aphæa or Dictynna

Aspledon.what: Aspledon, son of Poseidon, gives his name to the town

Asterius.what: Asterius, a giant, is buried on Lade

Attes.what: Attes is told of in the Lydian boar and Agdistis stories

Aurora.what: Aurora pleads with Zeus and Thetis for her son Memnon

Axion.what: Axion, son of Phegeus, kills Alcmæon

Battus.what: Battus, cured of speech trouble by fear of a lion, founds Cyrene

Briareus.what: Briareus arbitrates between Poseidon and the Sun over the Isthmus

Bunus.what: Bunus builds the temple of Bunæan Hera

Bupalus.what: Bupalus makes the first statue of Fortune

Buphagus.what: Buphagus nurses the wounded Iphicles at Pheneus

Callipatira.what: Callipatira sneaks into the Olympic games and is spared

Callipolis.what: Callipolis is killed by his father Alcathous

Callirhoe.what: Callirhoe rejects Coresus and is nearly sacrificed; she kills herself

Calus.what: Calus is murdered by his uncle Daedalus

Cephisodorus.what: Cephisodorus gathers allies against Philip and seeks Roman help

Chæron.what: Chæron, a wrestler, becomes tyrant of Pellene

Charon.what: Charon ferries the dead across Acheron in the painting

Cithæron.what: Cithæron advises Zeus to parade a wooden statue as a bride, reconciling Hera

Cleœtas.what: Cleœtas invents the staggered starting mechanism for the Olympic hippodrome

Colænus.what: Colaenus leads settlers from Attica, following a lark, to found Colonides

Coresus.what: Coresus, rejected by Callirhoe, prays to Dionysus and kills himself in her place

Corinna.what: Corinna, poetess of Tanagra, defeats Pindar and has a tomb and painting

Cranaus.what: Cranaus is expelled from the Athenian kingship by Amphictyon

Crocon.what: Crocon rules beyond the Rheti, in the war between Eleusis and Athens

Damagetus.what: Damagetus of Rhodes marries Aristomenes' daughter, where Aristomenes dies

Damasistratus.what: Damasistratus, king of Platæa, buries Laius at the Cross-roads

Daphne.what: Daphne, huntress, befriends the disguised Leucippus, who is killed when discovered bathing

Demophon.what: Demophon is the first man tried at the Palladium

Dinocrates.what: Dinocrates, newly elected, repels the Achaeans under Lycortas
Dinocrates poisons the captured Philopoemen at Messene

Dirce.what: Dirce, wife of Lycus, is killed by Antiope's sons and gives her name to the river

Eleus.what: Eleus and Augeas rule Elis, and Hercules is cheated of his reward

Emperamus.what: Emperamus's herdsman betrays the unguarded citadel to him in the rain
Emperamus leads the Spartan assault on Eira, fighting three days until Messenians retreat

Epebolus.what: Epebolus exposes the substituted maiden, forcing Aristodemus to offer his own daughter

Jocasta.what: Jocasta, wife of Laius, bears Oedipus, who kills his father and marries her

Erginus.what: Erginus beats Thebes, is defeated by Hercules, and late in life fathers Trophonius and Agamedes

Euæphnus.what: Euæphnus sells Polychares' cattle and kills his son, provoking the war

Euergetidas.what: Euergetidas dies in a last raid against the Spartans after Eira falls

Euippus.what: Euippus, the king's son, is devoured by the lion of Cithaeron

Eumenes.what: Eumenes hands the kingdom over to his cousin Attalus

Euphemus.what: Euphemus tells of the red-haired, tailed Satyrs on distant islands

Euphorbus.what: Euphorbus of Eretria is listed among Greek traitors who ruined their cities

Eupolemus.what: Eupolemus of Argos is the architect of the Heraeum temple

Euripides.what: Euripides, buried in Macedonia, is honoured by a cenotaph at Athens

Eurotas.what: Eurotas drains the plain and gives his name to the river

Euryleon.what: Euryleon commands the Spartan centre in the second campaign
Euryleon commands the Lacedaemonian centre in the indecisive night battle

Eurynome.what: Eurynome is worshipped at Phigalia; her temple opens once a year

Eurypon.what: Eurypon gives his name to the Eurypontid royal house

Eurysthenes.what: Eurysthenes and twin Procles found Sparta's two royal houses and colonize Thera

Euthymus.what: Euthymus fights the Hero of Temesa, drives it off and marries the maiden
Euthymus is beaten at boxing by Theagenes

Evander.what: Evander leads Arcadians from Pallantium to found a colony on the Tiber

Gitiadas.what: Gitiadas makes the bronze statue and temple of Athene Poliuchus at Sparta

Glauce.what: Glauce throws herself into a well, fearing Medea's poison

Gorgasus.what: Gorgasus is honoured at Pharae as a healer with Nicomachus

Gorgias.what: Gorgias of Leontini, the rhetorician, goes on embassy to Athens

Halirrhothius.what: Halirrhothius is killed by Ares, at the spring by Aesculapius' temple

Harmodius.what: Harmodius, with Aristogiton, kills Hipparchus and is honoured with a statue

Harpalus.what: Harpalus, fleeing Alexander, builds the grand tomb of Pythionice
Harpalus brings money from Asia; Demosthenes is cleared of taking it

Hecas.what: Hecas rotates Spartan reserves to wear out the Messenians at Eira

Helice.what: Helice marries Ion, who inherits the kingdom

Hermogenes.what: Hermogenes, the Lycian runner nicknamed Horse, wins Olympic running victories

Hero of Temesa.what: The Hero of Temesa demands a girl each year until Euthymus drives him off

Sibyl.what: The Sibyl chants on the Delphic rock and is buried in the Troad

Hilaira.what: Hilaira has a temple at Sparta shared with Phœbe

Hipparchus.what: Hipparchus, son of Pisistratus, is murdered

Hydarnes.what: Hydarnes outflanks the Greeks at Thermopylæ

Hydra.what: The Hydra is reared under the plane-tree at Amymone's spring

Hyettus.what: Hyettus flees Argos after killing Molurus for adultery

Hypsus.what: Hypsus, son of Lycaon, founds several Arcadian towns

Iccus.what: Iccus of Epidaurus is killed by Cleomedes in a boxing match

Isagoras.what: Isagoras seizes the Acropolis with Timasitheus' help

Ischepolis.what: Ischepolis dies in the Calydonian boar hunt, triggering Callipolis' death at his father's hand.

Itys.what: Itys is murdered by his mother Procne and her sister Philomela.

Lachares.what: Lachares rules Athens as a savage tyrant, is overthrown by Demetrius and killed in Boeotia.

Lamedon.what: Lamedon, king of Sicyon, surrenders Antiope to Thebes after the war.

Learchus.what: Learchus is killed by his father Athamas, as Ino leaps into the sea.

Leocritus.what: Leocritus is the first over the wall into the Museum in Olympiodorus' attack.

Lichas.what: Lichas deciphers an oracle and finds the bones of Orestes in a Tegean smithy.
Lichas is scourged for entering the games under Theban colours, causing the war at the Altis.

Linus.what: Linus, the musician, is killed by Apollo and mourned; Pausanias gives traditions of his death and burial.

Lydiades.what: Lydiades rules Megalopolis as an ambitious but patriotic tyrant and dies fighting.

Machanidas.what: Machanidas, Spartan tyrant, is killed by Philopoemen at Mantinea.

Magas.what: Magas revolts at Cyrene, marches on Egypt, then turns back when the Marmaridæ revolt.

Manticlus.what: Manticlus proposes Sardinia, helps take Zancle and builds a temple of Hercules.

Mantineus.what: Mantineus builds the town of Mantinea.

Medon.what: Medon is awarded the Athenian kingship by the Pythian Priestess over Nileus.

Megapenthes.what: Megapenthes swaps kingdoms with Perseus, who founds Mycenae.

Melia.what: Melia bears Apollo's sons Tenerus and Ismenius, after Caanthus is killed seeking her.

Minotaur.what: The Minotaur in the Labyrinth is tied to the bull and Minos' tribute.

Mopsus.what: Mopsus, son of Rhacius and Manto, expels the Carians from Claros.

Muses.what: The Muses defeat the Sirens in a singing contest, who lose their wings.

Mys.what: Mys receives an oracle answer in Carian at Ptoan Apollo's sanctuary.

Neocles.what: Neocles leads the Thebans to seize Platæa while its farmers are in the fields.

Nicomachus.what: Nicomachus is honoured as a healer at Pharae with his brother Gorgasus.

Nycteus.what: Nycteus, Theban regent, dies of wounds in the war over Antiope.

Nyctimus.what: Nyctimus inherits the kingdom of Arcadia from Lycaon.

Oebotas.what: Pausanias shows Oebotas could not have fought at Plataea.
Oebotas, unrewarded for his Olympic victory, curses the Achaeans; honours end the curse.

Orchomenus.what: Orchomenus gives his name to the town and gives Hyettus land.

Otilius.what: Otilius is sent against Philip and destroys Hestiaea and Anticyra.

Pæonius.what: Pæonius of Mendæ makes the Victory given by the Messenians.

Palamedes.what: Palamedes, inventor of dice, is shown in the painting; his drowning is told.

Pantaleon.what: Pantaleon rules Pisa in its contest with Elis over the games.

Pelopidas.what: Pelopidas is seized by Alexander of Pherae and freed by Epaminondas' rescue.

Penthesilea.what: Penthesilea, the Amazon, is shown scorning Paris in the painting.

Pergamus.what: Pergamus, youngest son of Pyrrhus, founds Pergamus.

Peribœa.what: Peribœa is the woman Minos desires, prompting his taunt of Theseus and the ring.

Persæus.what: Persæus, head of the Corinth garrison, is killed when Aratus wins Corinth.

Phaennis.what: Phaennis prophesies that the Galati will invade Asia and be destroyed by Attalus.

Phæstus.what: Phæstus introduces sacrifice to Hercules as a god at Sicyon.

Pharis.what: Pharis founds Pharae, and his daughter links to the line of Diocles.

Phayllus.what: Phayllus, Phocian commander, dreams of the wasted bronze old man and dies of wasting disease.

Phegeus.what: Phegeus gives his daughter to Alcmæon; his sons kill Alcmæon over the necklace.

Phemonoe.what: Phemonoe prophesies the punishment of the insolent son of Crius who plundered the temple.

Philæus.what: Philæus, son of Eurysaces, gives Salamis to Athens.

Philétærus.what: Philétærus, a Paphlagonian eunuch, revolts from Lysimachus, whose line leads to Attalus.
Philétærus gives Seleucus Pergamum and money, enabling Lysimachus's defeat.

Philip son of Demetrius.what: Philip son of Demetrius rules by bribery and poison, garrisoning Corinth, Chalcis and Magnesia.

Philippides.what: Philippides receives the message from Pan on his way to Lacedaemon.

Ptolemy Philometor.what: Ptolemy Philometor is exiled by his mother Cleopatra, returns and crushes the Thebans.

Phœbe.what: Phœbe is honoured with Hilaira in the temple of the Leucippides.

Pisirodus.what: Pisirodus wins at Olympia, and his mother Callipatira is spared for attending.

Pisus.what: Pisus is named as founder of Pisa.

Pityocamptes.what: Pityocamptes, the Pinebender robber, is killed by Theseus.

Pleistoanax.what: Pleistoanax, son of Pausanias, appears as Spartan king in the succession.

Plemnæus.what: Plemnæus builds the temple of Demeter in gratitude.

Podares.what: Podares falls fighting Epaminondas and is memorialised at Mantinea.

Polites.what: Polites of Ceramus is praised for his running victories at Olympia.

Polychares.what: Polychares, wronged by Euæphnus, who kills his son, goes mad and kills Spartans.
Sparta demands Polychares, and the Messenian kings split over surrendering him.

Polyxena.what: Polyxena is shown in a painting about to be sacrificed.

Protophanes.what: Protophanes of Magnesia is noted for his strange skeleton.

Psamathe.what: Psamathe bears Apollo's child, leading to Corœbus's killing of Punishment.

Pylas.what: Pylas bequeaths Megaris to Pandion in Megarian tradition.

Pytharatus.what: Pytharatus commands the Messenian cavalry and light troops at the ravine.
Pytharatus dies, and the Messenian wing collapses.

Pytheas.what: Pytheas, Bœotarch, incites Thebes to war against Rome.
Pytheas is executed by Metellus at Thebes.

Pythocles.what: Pythocles rebuilds the burned temple at Sicyon.

Rhacius.what: Rhacius settles Claros and marries Manto; their son Mopsus expels the Carians.

Scedasus.what: Scedasus kills himself after Spartans rape his daughters.

Scyllis.what: Scyllis the diver cuts Xerxes' ships' cables in a storm and is honoured.

Sicyon.what: Sicyon becomes king and gives the city his name.

Sicyonians.what: Sicyonians invade Ægira and are frightened off by torch-bearing goats.

Sosipolis.what: Sosipolis, a baby turned dragon, routs the Arcadians attacking Elis.
Sosipolis is honoured in his shrine at Elis.

Strato.what: Strato wins pancratium and wrestling on one day and gets a portico.

Sybotas.what: Sybotas decrees annual sacrifices to the dead king.

Taras.what: Taras is named as the hero of Tarentum, son of Poseidon, in the founding story.

Telesarchus.what: Telesarchus' garrison defeats the Galati attacking Athene's temple near Trachis, and he is killed.

Tellias.what: Tellias devises the night attack in which five hundred Phocians whiten themselves with plaster.

Tellis.what: Tellis rides in Charon's boat with Cleoboea in Polygnotus' painting of the underworld.

Theocosmus.what: Theocosmus makes the Zeus statue in the Olympieum, left unfinished because of the war with Athens.

Thucydides.what: Thucydides, son of Olorus, is recalled from exile and murdered.

Thyestes.what: Thyestes is buried near the road; his feud with Atreus is recounted.

Timasitheus.what: Timasitheus of Delphi joins Isagoras' seizure of the Acropolis and is executed by the Athenians.

Timosthenes.what: Timosthenes, priest of Hercules, is reputed father of Theagenes, whose boyhood feat is told.

Triton.what: Triton attacks women bathing before Dionysus' rites and is defeated by the god.
Triton raids herds and boats, is lured by wine, falls asleep and is beheaded.

Acarnanians.what: The Acarnanians besiege the Messenians at Œniadæ and force them into a blockade.
After eight months the Acarnanians' blockade is broken as the Messenians escape by night.

Æsymnetes.what: Æsymnetes' image in its chest is tended by nine men and nine women at the festival.

Æsymnus.what: Æsymnus consults Delphi after Hyperion's death; the Megarians build a council chamber over the heroes' tomb.

Ætolians.what: The Ætolians help the Messenians escape by night to Naupactus.

Agasisthenes.what: Agasisthenes persuades the 24 accused Spartans to go into exile.

Agias.what: The seer Agias foretells Lysander's capture of the Athenian fleet.

Agorius.what: Agorius and some Achæans settle in Elis at Oxylus's invitation, following an oracle.

Alcetas.what: Alcetas, son of Tharypus, appears in the Epirote royal line.
Alcetas rules madly and is killed; Pyrrhus is recalled.

Alcimedon.what: Alcimedon exposes his daughter Phialo and her baby by Hercules.

Alexander the Great.what: Alexander the Great is named as Lysimachus's master in the story of the lion.

Alphesibœa.what: Alphesibœa marries the mad Alcmæon, who later weds Callirhoe and is killed.

Anaximenes.what: Anaximenes saves Lampsacus from Alexander by asking him to do what he swore against.
Anaximenes forges a slanderous book in Theopompus's style, turning Greece against him.

Androclea.what: Androclea dies with her sister so that Thebes may win the war against Orchomenus.

Antipœnus.what: Antipœnus refuses to die for the people; his daughters die in his place.

Anyte.what: Anyte carries the sealed letter from Aesculapius to Phalysius, who is cured.

Apollonius.what: The boxer Apollonius is fined for arriving late and attacks Heraclides.

Appius.what: Appius judges for Sparta and has the Spartan exiles restored.
Appius favours the returning exiles, and the Senate orders their restoration.

Archidamea.what: The priestess Archidamea helps Aristomenes escape after the women of Ægila capture him.

Argæus.what: Ptolemy kills his brother Argæus for plotting against him.

Aristarchus.what: Aristarchus tells of the armoured dead man found in the roof of Hera's temple.

Aristomelidas.what: Aristomelidas seizes a Tegean maiden, who kills herself, and is later killed by Chronius.

Arrhachion.what: Arrhachion breaks his opponent's finger while dying and is crowned a posthumous Olympic victor.

Asteropea.what: Asteropea, with her sisters, is tricked by Medea into boiling Pelias, then flees to Arcadia.

Astrabacus.what: Astrabacus goes mad on finding the statue, which leads to the flogging ritual.

Astylus.what: Astylus is punished by Croton for running as a Syracusan.

Aura.what: The mare Aura wins her race after throwing her rider.

Bacchylides.what: Bacchylides casts the seventh Boeotarch vote for battle at Leuctra

Bathycles.what: Bathycles of Magnesia is the maker of the carved throne of Amyclaean Apollo

Baucis.what: Baucis' statue stands at Olympia beside Timanthes' and the Arcadian athletes'

Belistiche.what: Belistiche of Macedonia wins the colt-pair race

Bœus.what: Bœus founds Boeae after a hare leads settlers to the site

Bolgius.what: Bolgius leads a Celtic army, defeats and kills Ptolemy of Macedon

Bolina.what: Bolina flees Apollo and is made immortal

Bryas.what: Bryas outrages a maiden, causing the thousand picked men to be killed

Bulon.what: Bulon founds the colony of Bulis

Caanthus.what: Caanthus is killed by Apollo for burning his grove seeking Melia

Callistratus.what: Callistratus saves the Athenian cavalry at the Asinarus and dies fighting

Cambaules.what: Cambaules leads the first Celtic expedition into Greece

Carme.what: Britomartis flees Minos and becomes a goddess, per Carme's story

Carnus.what: Carnus, Acarnanian prophet of Apollo, is slain, explaining the Carnean cult

Cerynes.what: Cerynes tries to carry off Hyrnetho and is killed by Deiphontes

Chronius.what: Chronius, sent a dream by Artemis, kills the tyrant Aristomelidas and founds her temple

Chryseis.what: Chryseis, the priestess, falls asleep and her lamp burns down the old temple

Cleomedes.what: Cleomedes kills Iccus in a boxing match, goes mad, vanishes into a chest and is honoured as a hero

Cleonice.what: Cleonice is accidentally frightened and killed by the general Pausanias at Byzantium

Cleosthenes.what: Cleosthenes of Epidamnus becomes the first horse-owner to set up his own statue at Olympia

Cleostratus.what: Armed with a hooked breastplate by Menestratus, Cleostratus kills the dragon that demanded a youth yearly.

Clitomachus.what: Clitomachus asks for the pancratium to be called before boxing and loses to Caprus.

Comaetho.what: Comaetho, forbidden to marry, couples with Melanippus in Artemis's temple, bringing famine and plague.

Combutis.what: Combutis and Orestorius lead picked troops into Ætolia and sack Callion with horrible cruelty.

Comon.what: Comon leads the exiled Messenians to Libya and has a dream foretelling their return.

Creugas.what: Creugas is killed by Damoxenus's foul blow at Nemea and crowned posthumously.

Cyathus.what: Hercules strikes the cupbearer Cyathus dead, displeased with the drink; a chapel is built to him.

Cydias.what: Cydias, a young Athenian, dies in his first battle at Thermopylae; his shield is dedicated.

Damarmenus.what: Damarmenus, an Eretrian fisherman, fishes up Pelops' bone and gives it to the Eleans.

Damoclidas.what: Damoclidas is one of the Boeotarchs split over whether to fight at Leuctra.

Damocritus.what: Damocritus leads the Achaeans against Sparta, fails to follow up his win, is fined and flees.

Damoxenus.what: Damoxenus kills Creugas with a spear-hand blow at Nemea and is expelled.

Degmenus.what: Degmenus, the Elean bowman champion, is beaten in single combat by Pyræchmes.

Demetrius the son of Antigonus.what: Demetrius son of Antigonus overthrows Lachares and fortifies the Museum hill.

Demetrius the son of Phanostratus.what: Cassander makes Demetrius son of Phanostratus ruler of Athens.

Demophantus.what: Philopoemen kills the Elean cavalry commander Demophantus at the Larisus.

Diitrephes.what: Diitrephes' arrow-pierced statue recalls his Thracians' massacre at Mycalessus.

Dinomenes the Syracusan.what: Dinomenes the Syracusan kills Hiero II of Syracuse.

Dotadas.what: Dotadas promotes cults and builds a harbour at Mothone.

Dromichetes.what: Dromichetes and the Getae defeat Lysimachus, who makes peace.

Dropion.what: Dropion sends the bronze bison head to Delphi.

Echestratus.what: Echestratus is king of Sparta, and under him the Cynurians are expelled.

Eleans.what: The Eleans split into factions; pro-Spartans admit Messenian soldiers carrying Spartan-marked shields, who expel them.

Eperastus.what: Eperastus's inscription claims descent from Melampus, and Pausanias traces his seer family to Elis.

Ephesus.what: Ephesus is co-founder of the city that bears his name.

Epidaurus.what: Epaminondas's namesake aside, Epidaurus gives his name to the land, though his parentage is disputed.

Epiteles.what: Epiteles digs up the bronze urn holding the tin scroll of the Great Goddesses' mysteries.

Eratus.what: Eratus leads the Argives to take and raze Asine, sparing Apollo's temple.

Erythrus.what: Erythrus leads Cretans to found Erythrae, later joined by Lycians, Carians and Pamphylians.

Eupheme.what: Eupheme, nurse of the Muses, has her statue near the Aganippe spring on Helicon.

Eupolus.what: Eupolus, a Thessalian boxer, bribes his rivals, and the fine paid pays for Zanes statues of Zeus.

Eurydamidas.what: Eurydamidas, young king of the other Spartan house, is poisoned by Cleomenes.

Euryganea.what: Euryganea, daughter of Hyperphas, is argued to be the mother of Oedipus's children.

Eurynomus.what: Eurynomus, the Hades demon said to devour corpses, is painted by Polygnotus.

Eurysaces.what: Eurysaces, son of Ajax, is honoured at Athens alongside his father.

Eurytion.what: Eurytion the Centaur carries off Pirithous' wife in the west gable's battle.

Muiagrus.what: Muiagrus, the fly-driving god, receives first sacrifice at Aliphera so the people are free of flies.

Gaius.what: Gaius removes the Eros statue by Lysippus from Thespiae.

Gallus.what: Gallus, sent by Rome, scorns the Lacedaemonians and Argives and lets towns leave the Achaean League.

Gelanor.what: Gelanor competes with Danaus for the kingdom and loses after the wolf omen.

Gonippus.what: Gonippus and Panormus pose as Castor and Pollux and stab many Spartans at the feast.

Tanagra.what: Tanagra, wife of Pœmander, gives her name to the city.

Grais.what: Grais leads a fleet that settles Æolis under Agis.

Greeks.what: The Greeks, with Athenian ships, repulse Brennus's Galati at Thermopylae and bury their dead.

Heleus.what: Heleus founds Helus, whose fall to the Dorians gives the Helots their name.

Helle.what: Helle is saved with Phrixus from sacrifice by the golden ram.

Hemithea.what: Hemithea and Tennes, falsely accused, are cast to sea in a chest and reach Tenedos.

Hercyna.what: Hercyna, who played with Proserpine, gives her name to the river and the goose story.
