Herdsman.what: The herdsman seduces a Messenian's wife, overhears the guards' lapse and betrays Eira to Emperamus.

Hippasus.what: Hippasus's party flees the Dorians to Samos; Pythagoras descends from him.

Hippo.what: Hippo and her sister are raped by Spartans and hang themselves; Epaminondas honours them.

Hippolyta.what: Hippolyta flees to Megara after the Amazons' defeat and dies of grief.

Historis.what: Historis tricks the Sorceresses in the Theban tale of Hercules' madness.

Hyantes.what: The Hyantes flee Thebes and found Hyampolis.

Hydna.what: Hydna, with her father Scyllis, cuts Xerxes' ships' cables in a storm.

Hyrieus.what: Hyrieus has a treasury built, which Trophonius and Agamedes rob.

Iaseus.what: Iaseus appears bearded beside Phocus in the painting, his signet-ring scene explained.

Iodama.what: Iodama, priestess of Itonian Athene, is turned to stone on seeing Medusa's head.

Iphicles.what: Iphicles, wounded fighting Augeas, is brought to Pheneus, cared for, buried and honoured as hero.

Lais.what: Lais, the famous courtesan, has her tomb at Corinth and her origins are told.

Las.what: Las's killing is attributed by locals to Achilles, whom Pausanias denies was a suitor.

Leæna.what: Leæna is tortured to death by Hippias and honoured with a bronze lioness.

Lebadus.what: Lebadus, Athenian settler, gives Lebadea its name when the town moves to the plain.

Leonymus.what: Leonymus is healed on Leuce, sees Achilles and Helen, and carries her message to Stesichorus.

Lepreus.what: Lepreus eats against Hercules, then challenges him to arms and is killed.

Limon.what: Limon kills his brother Scephrus and is shot by Artemis, bringing famine.

Lophis.what: Lophis is killed by his father on Delphi's advice, and water gushes from his blood.

Lysippe.what: Lysippe, wife of Prolaus, curses Elis after her sons are killed at the Isthmus.

Macaria.what: Macaria dies willingly to win Athens victory over Eurystheus, protecting Hercules' children.

Phormis.what: Phormis, Arcadian soldier risen to fortune in Sicily, is honoured by offerings including bronze horses.

Marmaridæ.what: The Marmaridæ revolt from Magas, forcing him to turn back from marching on Egypt.

Marmax.what: Marmax, first suitor of Hippodamia, is killed by Oenomaus and buried in the suitors' tomb.

Meles.what: Meles, an Athenian youth, kills himself from remorse, leading to the cult of Anteros.

Meltas.what: Meltas, last king of Argos, is deposed by the Argives.

Menestratus.what: Menestratus arms his lover Cleostratus with a hooked breastplate to kill the dragon.

Menodorus.what: Menodorus makes a copy of the Eros statues burnt under Gaius and Nero.

Menœceus.what: Menœceus kills himself in obedience to the Delphic oracle; his tomb is shown.

Menophanes.what: Menophanes, Mithridates' general, sacks Delos and is punished by the god.

Mermerus.what: Mermerus, with his brother, is stoned by the Corinthians; his tomb stands on the Sicyon road.

Merope.what: Merope's husband Cresphontes is murdered by rebels, and her son Æpytus survives.

Metanira.what: Metanira receives Demeter, the old woman, into her house; her temple stands nearby.

Methapus.what: Methapus reforms the mysteries of the Great Goddesses, which are celebrated at Andania.

Micythus.what: Micythus dedicates many offerings at Olympia and vows for his sick son.

Milo.what: Milo of Croton wins victories, performs feats of strength and dies trapped in a split tree.

Moline.what: Moline seeks her sons' killer and curses those who attend the Isthmian games.

Molpia.what: Molpia is raped by Spartans with her sister and hangs herself.

Narcæus.what: Narcæus, son of Physcoa and Dionysus, builds a temple of Athene Narcaea.

Narcissus.what: Narcissus loves his own reflection at the Thespian fountain, in two versions.

Naupactians.what: The Messenians at Naupactus decide to fight the Acarnanians in the open at Œniadæ.

Nicagora.what: Nicagora brings Æsculapius from Epidaurus to Sicyon as a dragon.

Nicippe.what: Nicippe dedicates the statue of Aphrodite Symmachia at Mantinea.

Nileus.what: Nileus quarrels with Medon over the Athenian throne, loses, and leads the Ionian colony to Miletus.

Nymphs of the Aniger.what: The Nymphs of the Aniger cure lepers who pray, wipe their sores and swim the river.

Ocnus.what: Ocnus plaits rope that a she-ass eats, giving rise to the proverb.

Œniadæ.what: The Œniadæ are defeated by the Messenians and surrender their fort on terms.

Œnotrus.what: Œnotrus leads the first Greek colony to Italy.

Onomarchus.what: Onomarchus succeeds Philomelus, is beaten by Philip and killed by his own men.

Oresthasians.what: The 100 picked men of Oresthasium die fighting and win back Phigalia.

Orestorius.what: Orestorius and Combutis lead Galati into Ætolia and sack Callion with horrible cruelty.

Teuthis.what: Teuthis, angry with Agamemnon at Aulis, stabs Athene; his land suffers until she is appeased.

Panænus.what: Panænus, brother of Phidias, paints the mythological panels around Zeus's throne.

Panormus.what: Panormus and Gonippus pose as Castor and Pollux before the feasting Spartans and stab many.

Parnassus.what: Parnassus builds the oldest town at Delphi, destroyed later in Deucalion's flood.

Parphorus.what: Parphorus guides the Ionians who build Scyppius and then Clazomenae.

Parthenius.what: Parthenius violates the daughters of Scedasus, who hang themselves.

Patron.what: Patron leads the Lilaeans' rising against the garrison.

Pelarge.what: Pelarge restores the mysteries of the Cabiri after the Epigoni drove them out.

Pentathlus.what: Pentathlus leads Cnidian colonists from Pachynus to settle the Lipara islands.

Perdiccas.what: Perdiccas attacks Ptolemy in Egypt and is murdered.

Periphetes.what: Periphetes the club-wielding robber is killed by Theseus.

Peteus.what: Peteus leads the Athenians who settle Stiris.

Phalæcus.what: Phalæcus is deposed for taking sacred money, sails to Crete and dies besieging Cydonia.

Phalysius.what: Phalysius, nearly blind, is cured by Aesculapius through Anyte's sealed letter.

Psophis.what: Psophis, founder of the town, is given rival identities in local tradition.

Pheres.what: Pheres, son of Medea, is stoned by the Corinthians and buried near the Sicyon road.

Phialo.what: Phialo is exposed by her father Alcimedon with her baby and rescued by Hercules.

Phigalians.what: The Phigalians flee Sparta's capture of their town, then win it back through the 100 men of Oresthasium

Philhammon.what: Philhammon is said to have founded the rites at Lerna; his verses are doubted as too late

Philoxenus.what: Philoxenus' letters show Demosthenes took no money from Harpalus

Phineus.what: Phineus is shown on the chest as the sons of Boreas drive off the Harpies

Phocians.what: The Phocians, fined by the Amphictyonic Council, seize Delphi under Philomelus and fight Thebes in the Sacred War

Phrurarchidas.what: Phrurarchidas and another Spartan rape the daughters of Scedasus, who then hang themselves

Phylonome.what: Phylonome slanders Tennes, who is cast into the sea in a chest with Hemithea

Physcoa.what: Physcoa of Elis bears Narcæus to Dionysus and is honoured in the Elean dance

Phytalus.what: Phytalus receives Demeter as a guest and is given the fig tree

Pierus.what: Pierus changes the number and names of the Muses, making them nine

Pityreus.what: Pityreus yields the land to Deiphontes and the Argives

Pœmander.what: Pœmander founds Tanagra and marries Tanagra, who gives the city its name

Polemarchus.what: Polemarchus, a hotheaded Spartan, murders King Polydorus

Priestess of Hera.what: The priestess of Hera confesses the child was hers, clearing Lyciscus of treason.

Ptolemy Lightning.what: Ptolemy Lightning murders Seleucus at Lysimachia.

Punishment.what: Punishment, the child-snatching monster sent by Apollo, is killed by Corœbus.

Pylos.what: Pylos son of Cleson founds Pylos and is later expelled by Neleus.

Pyræchmes.what: Pyræchmes, Oxylus' slinger, beats Degmenus in single combat and wins Elis for Oxylus.

Rhegnidas.what: Rhegnidas marches the Dorians on Phlius, and the citizens split.

Rhœus.what: Rhœus helps lead the Phocians to victory and is honoured with a statue at Delphi.

Sandion.what: Sandion kills King Hyperion, leading to the council chamber over the heroes' tomb.

Saon.what: Saon follows bees into the ground and finds the oracle of Trophonius.

Sardus.what: Sardus leads Libyans to the island and gives Sardinia its name.

Saron.what: Saron drowns while chasing a stag.

Scephrus.what: Scephrus is killed by his brother Limon, leading to famine and a festival.

Scirus.what: Scirus, the Dodona prophet, dies fighting for Eleusis against Erechtheus.

Scylla.what: Scylla betrays her city and is betrayed by Minos.

Selemnus.what: Selemnus is turned into a river.

Sirens.what: The Sirens lose a singing contest to the Muses and lose their wings.

Sotades.what: Sotades changes his city for a bribe and is exiled.

Sphinx.what: The Sphinx is variously described as a riddling monster, pirate or Laius's daughter, defeated by Oedipus.

Taurosthenes.what: Taurosthenes, Æginetan wrestler, wins, and his apparition announces the victory at Ægina.

Tennes.what: Tennes, falsely accused by his stepmother, is cast to sea and cuts his father's ropes with an axe.

Thessalonice.what: Thessalonice, Cassander's wife, is killed by her son Antipater.

Timagoras.what: Timagoras, a resident alien, leaps from the rock for Meles, giving rise to the cult of Anteros.

Timanthes.what: Timanthes burns himself alive when he can no longer bend his bow.

Tisias.what: Tisias goes with Gorgias on the embassy to Athens.

Tisis.what: Tisis is sent to Delphi, is ambushed on his return, delivers the oracle to the king and dies.

Tissaphernes.what: Tissaphernes is defeated by Agesilaus near the Hermus and later executed.

Tithraustes.what: Tithraustes replaces Tissaphernes and bribes Greek politicians, which leads Sparta into war with Thebes.

Tolmides.what: Tolmides campaigns as Athenian admiral and is killed at Haliartia.

Xenarches.what: Xenarches, first Acarnanian to win at Olympia, is honoured with a statue.

Xeno.what: Xeno offers to be tried, which the senator uses to send the accused to Rome.

Xenoclea.what: Xenoclea refuses Hercules an oracle because of Iphitus's murder, so he carries off the tripod.

Achelous.what: Achelous is shown fighting Hercules on the Megarian treasury.

Hieronymus.what: Hieronymus's claim that Lysimachus desecrated Epirote royal tombs is doubted by Pausanias.

Pittheus.what: Pittheus rules Trœzen, where the young Theseus lifts the stone.

Lampis.what: Lampis joins the four men who depose the tyrant Aristotimus.

Pentheus.what: Pentheus is torn apart after spying on the women; Dionysus statues made from his tree.

Phylas.what: King of the Dryopes, is defeated by Hercules, who then carries off the Dryopes.

Plato.what: Is buried near the Academy; Socrates' swan dream foretells his coming as pupil.

Sacadas.what: The flute-player Sacadas is buried near the gymnasium of Cylarabis.

Sciron.what: Sciron is thrown into the sea by Theseus.
Sciron the brigand is punished by Theseus; his road is built and later widened.

Socrates.what: Socrates dreams of a swan before Plato becomes his pupil.

Talthybius.what: Talthybius' wrath falls on Sparta after the murder of Darius' envoys; his tomb is shown.

Tegeates.what: Tegeates is father of Scephrus and Limon, whose tragedy brings famine to Tegea.

Tydeus.what: Tydeus, attacker of Thebes, is buried near the gate Proetis.

Acichorius.what: Acichorius commands a division of Celts, harassed by the Aetolians on the march to Delphi.

Actor.what: Actor's sons are ambushed and killed by Hercules at Cleonæ, provoking Moline's curse.

Athenians.what: Athenian triremes help the Greeks repulse the Galati at Thermopylae.

Car.what: Car is traced by the Megarians as early king who gave Megara its name.
Car gives the Megarian Acropolis its name.

Cephalus.what: Cephalus, exile who settled Cephallenia, has descendants who found a temple of Apollo.

Diocles.what: Diocles' grandsons Nicomachus and Gorgasus are honoured as healers at Pharae.

Diogenes.what: Diogenes the Cynic is buried at the gate on the road to Corinth.

Hyperochus.what: Hyperochus' apparition appears in the battle against the Celts at Delphi.

Ladon.what: The Ladon is praised as the most beautiful stream in Greece.

Mnaseas.what: Mnaseas, hoplite runner of Cyrene, has his victor statue listed among the Olympia boxers and runners.

Mæra.what: Mæra's tomb near Mantinea is noted on the road to Orchomenus, with Anchises' tomb.
Maera is painted in the underworld at Delphi beside Actaeon and his mother.

Mecisteus.what: Mecisteus, Adrastus' brother, is slain by Melanippus; his tomb stands on the Chalcis road.

Melaneus.what: Melaneus, the archer, comes to Perieres and receives Carnasium, once called Œchalia.

Mico.what: Mico makes the statues of Hiero II of Syracuse at Olympia.

Myles.what: Myles rules Laconia as Lelex's son, with Eurotas and Lacedaemon after.
Myles is credited with inventing mills at Alesiae.

Mysius.what: Mysius is the host who received Demeter, in the Hermione founding legend.

Nicander.what: Nicander, Spartan king, invades Argolis; Asine sides with Sparta and is later razed by Argives.

Omphalion.what: Omphalion paints the Messenian kings and heroes shown in Messene.

Orithyia.what: Orithyia is carried off by the North Wind near the Ilissus.

Otus.what: Otus, a giant slain by Apollo, has his tomb at Anthedon with Ephialtes.
Otus and Ephialtes found the cult of the Muses and the town Ascra.

Pandrosus.what: Pandrosus obeys Athene and does not open the chest.

Periander.what: Periander is compared with the Pisistratidæ in the account of Leæna's torture.
Periander is named among the Seven Wise Men whose sayings the vestibule bears.

Perilaus.what: Perilaus the Argive wrestler is shown slaying Othryades in a monument.
Perilaus accuses Orestes of killing his mother.

Phigalus.what: Phigalus, son of Lycaon, founds and names Phigalia.

Philammon.what: Philammon fights the Phlegyans at Delphi and dies.
Philammon wins the early hymn contest at Delphi.

Phlias.what: Phlias gives his name to Phliasia; his parentage is argued.

Phrixus.what: Phrixus and Helle are saved from sacrifice by the golden ram.

Phylacus.what: Phylacus appears as a hero fighting the Gauls at Delphi.

Schedius.what: Schedius sits with Orpheus in the willow grove of the painting.
Schedius, son of Iphitus, dies in the Troad; his tomb is at Anticyra.

Actaeus.what: Actaeus is first king of Attica, followed by Cecrops.

Adimantus.what: Adimantus is accused of being bribed by Lysander at Aegospotami.

Aetius.what: Aetius, son of Anthas, builds the temple of Zeus Soter.

Aglaurus.what: Aglaurus opens the chest and throws herself from the Acropolis.

Althæa.what: Althæa is shown as Meleager's mother who burned the firebrand.

Althepus.what: Althepus, son of Poseidon, is an early king of Trœzen.

Androdamas.what: Androdamas succeeds as king of Sicyon, son of Phlias.

Andropompus.what: Andropompus is father of Melanthus, who leads Ionians to Attica.

Androtion.what: Androtion is cited for Dorieus's capture and execution by Sparta.

Argos.what: Argos becomes king, gives his name to the city, and begins the Argive royal line.

Aristion.what: Aristion, envoy of Mithridates, holds Athens against Sulla and is killed after its capture.

Corinthus.what: Corinthus, son of Marathon, gives his name to Corinth in the founding legends.

Enyalius.what: Enyalius is shown as a fettered statue at Sparta.

Eucles.what: Eucles, son of Callianax and Callipatira, is a boxer whose statue stands with his family's at Olympia.

Graces.what: The Graces have a temple with wooden statues at Elis.

Menander.what: Menander, poet son of Diopeithes, has his tomb on the road from the Piraeus.

Sophocles.what: Sophocles' statue stands in the theatre and tales of his dream-fed rival are told.

Thisoa.what: Thisoa, with Neda and Hagno, nurses the infant Zeus on Mount Lycæus.

Aenetus.what: Aenetus's statue at Amyclae commemorates the pentathlon victor who died after being crowned.

Aerope.what: Aerope dies in childbirth, and Ares fathers her child, giving rise to the name Aphneus.

Aganippe.what: The spring Aganippe, daughter of Termesus, is passed on the road to the Muses' grove.

Agdistis.what: Agdistis is born as a hermaphrodite from Zeus's seed, in the legend of Attes.

Aglaus.what: Aglaus of Psophis is said to be happy all his life; Pausanias doubts the tale.

Miletus.what: Miletus, a Cretan leader, gives his name to the city whose early history is told.

Anthemocritus.what: Anthemocritus, an Athenian herald, is killed by the Megarians and buried on the Sacred Way.

Antinous.what: Antinous, Hadrian's beloved, is worshipped as a god at Mantinea.

Aresthanas.what: Aresthanas, the goat-herd, finds the exposed child Æsculapius and sees lightning flash from him.

Argiope.what: Argiope is named as mother of the blinded singer Thamyris.

Carneus.what: Carneus is honoured at Sparta as Carnean Apollo, with rival stories of his cult's origin.

Circe.what: Circe appears on the chest's top side with Odysseus and four handmaids.

Cleander.what: Cleander, Mantinean exile, raises the orphaned Philopoemen.

Cleopus.what: Cleopus reorganizes the mixed colony of Erythrae.

Colontas.what: Colontas refuses Demeter hospitality and is burnt, leading to the temple's founding.

Dætus.what: Dætus, descended from Cephalus, helps found a temple of Apollo near Pythionice's tomb

Daiphantes.what: Daiphantes helps lead the Phocians to victory over the Thessalians

Damarchus.what: Damarchus the boxer is said to have turned into a wolf; Pausanias doubts it

Damiscus.what: Damiscus, a Messenian boy of twelve, wins the foot-race at Olympia

Damonicus.what: Damonicus of Elis bribes opponents for his son, and is fined

Daulis.what: Daulis, the nymph, gives her name to the town of Daulis

Demylus.what: Demylus sends his son Glaucus to Olympia and urges him to remember the ploughshare

Dicon.what: Dicon, the Caulonian runner, changes his city for money

Didas.what: Didas, an Egyptian boxer, takes a bribe and is fined

Dinomenes son of Hiero.what: Dinomenes dedicates a bronze chariot at Olympia honouring his father Hiero's victories

Eumœlus.what: Eumœlus' poetic account of Medea's flight, her son and her rule at Corinth is given

Euryclides.what: Euryclides, an Athenian orator, is poisoned by Philip

Euthymenes.what: Euthymenes is listed among Arcadian athletes with a statue at Olympia

Hannibal.what: Hannibal is deceived by an oracle's place name, Libyssa

Hermion.what: Hermion is discussed as founder of old Hermione, with Europs and Phoroneus

Hicetas.what: Hicetas takes Spartan bribes, betrays the Messenians, and is stoned, ending the dynasty.

Hiero son of Hierocles.what: Hiero son of Hierocles becomes tyrant, allies with Pyrrhus, then joins Rome and is killed by Dinomenes.

Hymnian Artemis.what: Hymnian Artemis has a temple whose priestess and priest live apart in strict purity.

Hypatus.what: Hypatus leads the Thebans as Boeotarch, but the army trapped at Pylae turns to Epaminondas.

Hyperesians.what: The Hyperesians' Hyperesia becomes Ægira when torch-bearing goats frighten off the Sicyonian invaders.

Hyperion.what: King Hyperion is killed, after which the Megarians build a council chamber over the heroes' tomb.

Hypermenides.what: Hypermenides leads the Corinthians, whose camp Aristomenes slaughters in a night attack.

Hysmon.what: Hysmon's statue is described; his training cured an illness.

Ictinus.what: Ictinus builds the beautiful temple of Apollo the Helper at Bassæ.

Injustice.what: Injustice, an ugly woman, is beaten by Justice on the chest.

Ismenias.what: Ismenias takes Persian gold from Tithraustes to stir up Greece against Sparta.

Ithome.what: Nymph Ithome nursed Zeus and gave her name to the mountain.

Julius Cæsar.what: Julius Cæsar resettles Corinth after its destruction by Mummius.

Justice.what: Justice, a beautiful woman, punishes Injustice in a scene on the chest.

Labotas.what: Under Labotas, with Lycurgus as regent, Sparta first fights Argos.

Leocydes.what: Leocydes' ancestor Arcesilaus is said to have seen an ancient stag with a collar.

Mera.what: Is sacrificed with Tegeates; the Tegeans commemorate this in a festival.

Midas.what: Midas, son of Gordias, builds Ancyra, which the Galati later capture.

Mnesibulus.what: Mnesibulus fights the Costoboci and wins races; his statue stands at Elatea.

Molossus.what: Molossus, son of Pyrrhus, inherits the kingdom of Epirus.

Mothone.what: Mothone, daughter of Oeneus, is said to have given the town its name.

Naus.what: Naus, descendant of Eumolpus, brings the Eleusinian mysteries to Pheneus.

Œnopion.what: Œnopion, a Cretan, settles Chios as its king.

Olæas.what: Olæas restores the blinded Æpytus to the throne of Messene.

Opheltes.what: Opheltes, child devoured by a dragon at Nemea, has his tomb there.

Opis.what: Opis, king of the Iapyges, is shown dying in the Tarentine group.

Orsobia.what: Orsobia, daughter of Deiphontes, is wife of Pamphylus; her sister Hyrnetho is killed.

Orus.what: Orus reigns as early king of Trœzen when Athene and Poseidon share the land.

Paeon.what: Paeon leaves Elis after his brother Epeus wins the kingdom, naming Paeonia.

Pronomus.what: Pronomus's flute-playing innovations are described and his statue stands beside Epaminondas's in Thebes.

Selinus.what: As king of the Ægialians, Selinus sees Ion marry his daughter Helice and inherit his kingdom.

Seres.what: The Seres obtain silk from an insect they rear, and Pausanias debates their race.

Sidectus.what: Sidectus, a Corinthian leader, is killed when Aristomenes slaughters the Corinthian camp at night.

Timoclidas.what: Timoclidas is among the usurpers who seize power at Sicyon before Aratus.

Neoptolemus.what: Pyrrhus helps Lysimachus keep Thrace, then is driven out of Macedonia.
Pyrrhus's lineage from Achilles' son is traced and he is recalled to rule Epirus.
Pyrrhus crosses to Italy at Tarentum's call and routs the Romans with elephants.
Pyrrhus goes to Sicily and forces the Carthaginians to lift the siege of Syracuse.
Pyrrhus slips away from Italy by night, then defeats Antigonus and conquers Macedonia.
Pyrrhus attacks Sparta at Cleonymus's urging, then is killed by a tile at Argos.
Pyrrhus leads Pisa's rebellion against Elis until the city is razed.

Hercules, Idaean Dactyl.what: As an infant Idaean Dactyl Hercules, he steals Zeus away from Cronos's fear on Ithome.
